## D-0244 · ARCH-005 — local-model-runtime's `launch()` can no longer authorise itself — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** `D-0242` left `ARCH-005` as the one remaining open item from `D-0240`'s
three-way question (the other two, `INST-004` and the `codev` split, closed as `D-0241`/
`D-0242`). `03_ARCHITETTURA.md` §4: "no adapter may grant itself a permission — a manifest
is a request, the engine issues the tokens." `capability.mjs`'s own `capabilityStatus()`
already asserted `adaptersMaySelfGrant: false` — a claim with no adapter behind it, because
until this phase no adapter existed that was wired to the engine at all.
`local-model-runtime.mjs` is the one adapter that exists (`03 §6`: the other six —
`VectorStoreAdapter`, `ObjectStoreAdapter`, `IndustryModuleProvider`,
`CompliancePackProvider`, `HostBridgeAdapter`, and a second `ModelRuntimeAdapter` for a
different accelerator — are not built), and its `launch()` method — the one call that
spawns a real OS process and hands it GPU access — ran on nothing stronger than the
`model.manage` RBAC permission already gating the HTTP route. That is a session-level
"can this user press the button", not the plan-approved, auditable, single-use token the
architecture means by "the engine issues the tokens" — and `launch()` itself had no way to
refuse a call that reached it by any other path than the one HTTP route.

**Built, not improvised.** New `services/reference-control-plane/src/adapter-capability.mjs`:
`ADAPTER_MANIFESTS` (today: `{'local-model-runtime': {operations: ['EXECUTE']}}` — the
manifest 03 §4 means, a fixed list of what a resource may ever ask for) and
`AdapterGrantOrchestrator`, which mirrors `workspace-actions.mjs`'s `plan()`/`approve()`
shape (`request()` builds a one-step plan naming the resource, `approve()` calls the SAME
`authorizePlan()`/`TokenMinter.mint()` workspace-actions spends through — no second engine,
no new operation type; `EXECUTE` already exists in `capability.mjs` and already means
"arbitrary code execution"). `local-model-runtime.mjs`'s `launch()` now takes a
`{capabilityToken}` and spends it against the same minter before doing anything else;
with no minter wired in at all it refuses outright rather than falling open (`config`
absent is treated as "no possible token", not "no gate").

**Routes** (`server.mjs`, same `model.manage` permission + CSRF as the existing
local-model routes): `GET /api/v1/adapters` (manifest + status), `POST /api/v1/adapters/
:resource/grants` (request), `POST /api/v1/adapters/grants/:runId/approve|reject`. `POST
/api/v1/runtime/local-model/launch` now forwards `capabilityToken` from the request body
instead of calling `launch()` with nothing.

**Verified, not assumed**: 26 new tests (7 in `local-model-runtime.test.mjs` — refuses
with no engine wired, refuses with no token, refuses a forged token [one flipped MAC
byte], refuses a different minter's token, a granted token is spent and cannot be
replayed, an out-of-manifest ask is refused, an unknown adapter is refused; 12 in the new
`adapter-capability.test.mjs`; 7 in the new `adapter-capability-http-adversarial.test.mjs`
— real HTTP routes, real session+CSRF, negative control proves the legitimate
request→approve→launch→release flow still works and the spent token cannot relaunch).
Unit **1155/1155** (+26), ESLint 235 files 0 errors, `scripts/test.sh` 10/10,
`auth-http-smoke` PASS. `MANIFEST.sha256` **5841/5841** (3 files re-hashed, 3 new files
added: `adapter-capability.mjs` + its 2 test files).

**Deployed live** (`noesar-evolution:phase4-arch005-adapter-gate`, `FROM
phase4-codev-peer` — no Rust changed this phase, so no rebuild of the supervisor stage,
only `services/reference-control-plane/` re-copied): image bytes proved identical to the
tree before touching production; `docker stop -t 60` with `postgres.stopped clean:true`
read in the log; runtime backup 12.5 MB
(`BACKUPS/runtime_pre_arch005_deploy_20260730T074008Z.tar.gz`); predecessor renamed to
rollback; new container started with every env/mount/network/port/hardening flag
re-read from the replaced container's own `docker inspect`. **Verified live**: `Up
(healthy)`, `RestartCount=0`, all `INST-004` hardening fields intact
(`ReadonlyRootfs:true`, `CapDrop:[ALL]`, `PidsLimit:512`), `/livez`+`/readyz` 200,
`GET /api/v1/adapters` 401 vs `/api/v1/does-not-exist` 404, process tree from `/proc`
still shows the three `D-0242` peers (`postgres`/`codev`/`api`, all `ppid=1`),
`migrations":16` (0 re-run), `data-plane.identity-projected: projected:1`.

**Reachability, stated rather than left implicit**: the live container runs with
`NOESAR_LOCAL_MODEL_RUNTIME=disabled` (administrative override — GPU runtime is off at
this deployment regardless of stored config), so `launch()` refuses at the `disabled`
check before it ever reaches the capability gate added here. The gate is real and is
exercised by the test suite above; on THIS deployment it has nothing to guard yet because
the feature it guards is itself switched off. Not a discrepancy — `config()`'s own
environment-override rule (`local-model-runtime.mjs`, documented since it was built)
already made `disabled` win over any stored mode.

**Not done, named rather than implied**: `attach()`, `complete()` and `configure()` on
this same adapter remain ungated — this phase's manifest covers `launch()` only, the one
method that spawns a process; a Network Egress Broker (the architecture's own separate
concept, `03 §3`) does not exist yet, so gating `attach()`/`complete()` today would either
reuse `EXECUTE` for something that is not process execution or invent a second operation
type — both named here as the wrong shortcut rather than taken. No WebUI surface calls the
new routes yet (same posture `D-0222`'s research-gate declared: built and tested at the
API layer, no button wired). `ARCH-005`'s acceptance criterion in `03_ARCHITETTURA.md`
("test that an adapter requests a permission not granted and is refused") is met for the
one adapter that exists; the other six adapters named in `03 §4` still do not exist, so
their manifests are not written and `ADAPTER_MANIFESTS` is not claimed to cover them.
**§5a**: two project containers (installation + one rollback, the most recent). Older
rollback `rollback-codev-peer-20260730T040708Z` removed after health confirmed, image
intact on disk. Networks (10) unchanged.
**Costo di rollback**: nessuno — nessuna migrazione, `AI_STATE_VERSION` invariato.
Returning to `:phase4-codev-peer` removes the capability gate on `launch()` — the adapter
would answer to `model.manage` RBAC alone again, nothing else.

## D-0245 · ARCH-007 — the Update Trust Verifier: a permission diff, enforced not just described — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** `03_ARCHITETTURA.md` §8 / `08_INSTALLAZIONE.md` §9 name the missing piece
under "Aggiornamenti": "**diff dei permessi** — un aggiornamento che chiede più autorità di
quella che aveva prima deve dirlo esplicitamente, e va autorizzato di nuovo." `INST-008`
already had signature/provenance tooling (`D-0208`: `cbom.mjs`, `generate-mlbom.mjs`,
`sign/verify-release-artifact.mjs`) but the permission-diff half was `⏳`/`⚠ parziale` —
named, never built. `ARCH-007`'s own acceptance test is explicit: "a package that widens
scope, verify it is blocked without new authorisation" — that needed a real mechanism to
run the verb against, not a description of one.

**Built**: new `services/reference-control-plane/src/permission-surface.mjs` — a
"permission surface" is the RBAC permission strings `server.mjs`'s own routes gate on
(`requireSession(req, res, '...')` / `auth.hasPermission(user, '...')`, extracted from
source text, the same declared-not-executed posture `generate-inventory.mjs` already uses)
plus the adapter capabilities `ADAPTER_MANIFESTS` (`D-0244`) lists. `diffPermissionSurfaces()`
compares two surfaces; `verifyUpdateAuthorized()` is the enforcement point: shrinking
authority never needs re-authorisation, widening it does, and the authorisation must name
**exactly** the tokens being added — not a subset (misses something) and not a superset
either (an authorisation broader than the actual change is not a description of what
happened, the same "widening is the whole attack" reasoning `capability.mjs`'s `mint()`
already applies to a step's declared files). Same approver/expiry discipline as
`authorizePlan()` throughout the rest of the engine — no second authorisation model
invented. Two CLI wrappers, mirroring the existing `sign`/`verify-release-artifact.mjs`
pattern: `tools/generate-permission-surface.mjs` (emits the current codebase's surface,
optionally signed via the same `signCompliancePack()` primitive `D-0208`'s tooling
reuses) and `tools/verify-permission-diff.mjs` (the Update Trust Verifier itself —
`--baseline`/`--candidate`/`--authorization`, exit 0 or 1).

**Verified, not assumed**: 13 new unit tests (extraction against synthetic source AND
against the real `server.mjs` — 18 real permissions found, not a placeholder count;
shrinking needs no authorisation; widening RBAC or adapter scope alike is refused with no
authorisation; a wrong-scoped authorisation does not rescue it; a superset authorisation is
refused, not accepted; expired or unnamed-approver authorisations refused). **End-to-end
against the real codebase, not only fixtures**: generated the actual current permission
surface (18 RBAC permissions + 1 adapter capability) with `generate-permission-surface.mjs`,
built a synthetic candidate adding 2 permissions, and ran the real CLI three times — refused
with no authorisation, refused with a wrong-scoped one, accepted only once the
authorisation named exactly the 2 added tokens. Unit **1168/1168** (+13), ESLint 239 files
0 errors, `scripts/test.sh` 10/10, `auth-http-smoke` PASS. `MANIFEST.sha256` **5845/5845**
(also caught and fixed a carried-over gap: `MASTER_PROJECT/03_ARCHITETTURA.md`'s hash had
gone stale after `D-0244`'s own edit to the `ARCH-005` row and was never refreshed — fixed
here alongside this phase's own edits, not a new problem, a previously-undetected one).

**No container rebuild or redeploy this phase**: these are release/update-time tools, read
by nothing at runtime — `server.mjs` does not import `permission-surface.mjs`, same
posture `D-0208`'s CBOM/ML-BOM/signing tools already have (verified against a live image
from the host, never copied into or run inside the container). `INST-008`'s own criterion
moves from `⚠ parziale` to `⚠ quasi completo`: signature, provenance and the permission
diff all exist and are proven; what remains is wiring them into one update pipeline instead
of two separate CLI invocations — named as the gap, not built here.

**Not done, named rather than implied**: there is no automated installer that ingests an
update package and calls this tool automatically — updates today are the manual `D-0143`
stop/backup/rollback/redeploy sequence a person drives, and this tool is what that person
(or a future installer) is expected to run before promoting a candidate, not something that
runs itself. No baseline permission surface is persisted anywhere yet as "the currently
installed one" — a future phase wiring an actual update pipeline needs to decide where that
baseline lives and how it gets refreshed after every legitimate deploy. `ARCH-008` (isolamento
per-capacità) remains open, addressed separately in this same session.

## D-0246 · ARCH-008 investigated on the real host — two of three mechanisms concretely blocked, not "never treated" for lack of trying — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** `ARCH-008` ("ogni capacità gira con i suoi limiti, non con quelli del
container intero" — Landlock, seccomp per profile, cgroups v2) has been `⏳`/"Alto risk
mai trattato" across many prior sessions. Rather than carry that forward again unexamined,
this phase actually tested each of the three named mechanisms against THIS host, in a
disposable container built and probed offline (never touching the production container or
its running data), and found a concrete, mostly negative answer — worth recording
precisely, because "not built" and "not buildable here without a larger decision" are
different facts and this backlog item had never distinguished them.

**Landlock — blocked at the kernel, not fixable in code.** A minimal Rust probe
(`libc::syscall(444, …)`, the `landlock_create_ruleset` ABI-version query, built offline
from the already-vendored `libc` crate — no new dependency) was run both unrestricted and
under the exact production hardening profile (`--cap-drop ALL --security-opt
no-new-privileges:true --user 10001:10001`, default Docker seccomp). Both return `errno=38
(ENOSYS)` — the kernel itself does not implement the syscall, which is what happens when
`CONFIG_SECURITY_LANDLOCK` is not compiled into the running kernel, independent of kernel
*version* (this host runs 6.18.38, years newer than Landlock's 5.13 introduction — the gap
is a build-time kernel config choice on this Unraid host, not an update owed). Fixing this
would mean replacing the host's kernel, an operating-system-level change on the physical
host this project has never been authorised to make and should not attempt unprompted.

**cgroups v2 per-capability limits — blocked by delegation, not code either.** `/sys/fs/cgroup`
is mounted (cgroup2, controllers `cpuset cpu io memory hugetlb pids` all listed) inside the
live container, which looked promising, but every write attempt refuses
(`Read-only file system`) — confirmed independent of the container's own `--read-only`
rootfs flag (tested again without it: identical refusal). Docker is not delegating a
writable cgroup subtree to this container. Granting one is a Docker daemon / cgroup driver
configuration decision made when a container is created, not something the process inside
it can arrange for itself.

**seccomp self-narrowing — the one mechanism confirmed genuinely available, and the one
that exposes the real remaining gap.** `prctl(PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS, 1, …)` succeeds
(`errno=0`) under the identical hardened profile — a process narrowing its OWN syscall
filter has always been permitted on any Linux kernel with seccomp (which this host plainly
has: `Seccomp: 2` already shows in `/proc/self/status` for Docker's own default profile).
But a seccomp filter, once installed, applies for the life of the THREAD that installed it
and can only ever get stricter, never lifted — and this product is one long-lived Node.js
process serving every request on one event loop. Installing a capability-specific filter
inside that process would narrow it for every OTHER request too, permanently, which is not
"per-capability" isolation, it is "isolate once and never serve anything wider again."
**The actual prerequisite this reveals**: per-capability isolation of any kind needs a
Sandbox Manager that is a real, separate process per spend (fork/exec a short-lived child
that installs its own seccomp profile — and Landlock/cgroups too, on a host where those are
available — does the one write or launch, and exits) — a concept `03_ARCHITETTURA.md §3`
already names, and which nothing in the product builds today: `executor.mjs` and the new
adapter-capability gate (`D-0244`) both spend tokens and act **in-process**.

**Not done, and not fabricated as done**: no code changed this phase. Building a real
per-spend sandboxed child-process executor is a genuine architectural addition — comparable
in scope to `ARCH-001`'s supervisor work, not a patch — and doing it hastily inside an
already-long session, on top of `D-0244`/`D-0245`, would be exactly the kind of rushed,
unverified claim this project's own rules forbid. Two of the three named mechanisms are
concretely blocked on THIS host without an infrastructure decision (kernel rebuild; Docker
cgroup delegation) neither authorised nor safely reversible to make unprompted. The third
is real but needs the sandbox-executor prerequisite first. **Recommendation, not a
decision made here**: either (a) the Owner authorises the host-level changes (kernel with
Landlock, delegated cgroups) so the eventual sandbox executor has all three primitives to
use, or (b) a dedicated future phase builds the child-process sandbox executor scoped to
seccomp only, with Landlock/cgroups added later if/when the host permits them — named as
two different, Owner-level choices, not defaulted to either silently.

## D-0247 · Le due leggi dell'Owner scritte nell'autorità e nelle skill; sei difetti delle skill riparati — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** `CLAUDE10.md` §16 (legge di piattaforma: self-hosted su qualunque PC/server/OS, l'host non è il prodotto, una modifica all'host non è mai un rimedio, le capacità si rilevano/degradano/dichiarano) e §17 (dovere di avanzamento: il criterio è la soglia, ogni fase produce una proposta di miglioramento, il metro è esterno), regole 60-69. Le stesse due leggi scritte nelle quattro skill, con il confine esplicito che vieta all'obbligo di migliorare di allargare la fase in corso.
**Why.** Ordine diretto dell'Owner dopo un mio errore reale: avevo chiesto di scegliere fra autorizzare cambi al kernel/Docker di questo host Unraid e una fase dedicata, trattando i limiti di UN host come un bivio di progetto. `ARCH-008` non era un bivio: l'opzione host è vietata per costruzione.
**Rejected.** Scrivere le leggi solo nelle skill: `CLAUDE10.md` vince sulle skill dove sono in conflitto, e infatti mandava ancora di avviare `noesar-debuglab` — la riparazione nelle skill sarebbe stata sovrascritta dall'autorità.
**Evidence.** Sei difetti trovati verificando meccanicamente ogni affermazione delle skill, non leggendole: (S-1/S-2) il passo obbligatorio HUNT AND FIX ordinava di avviare `noesar-debuglab` `:8099` — container **e** immagine inesistenti, porta morta, ed era host-coupled; sostituito da strumenti del repository + container usa-e-getta offline, provato dal vivo (`docker run --rm --network none -v repo:ro python:3-slim` → 4/4 PASS); (S-3) ogni riga della tabella delle dimensioni stale, `DECISION_LOG.md` +129% (160→367 KB), `MASTER_PROJECT` 14→16 doc; (S-4) il digest era 18.516 byte contro i 6,3 KB dichiarati perché `product_test_suite` aveva raggiunto 39 voci / 11,4 KB stampate intere (62% dell'output) → riparato a **10.279 byte, −44,5%**, con escape hatch `DIGEST_SUITE_ENTRIES=0`; (S-5) cap dell'handoff ≤150 righe mai misurato, era **382** → **133**; (S-6) le due leggi assenti. Misurato in sessione: unit **1168/1168**, ESLint **239 file 0 errori**, `verify-source` PASS, `MANIFEST` **5845/5845** contato riga per riga.
**Reversal cost.** Nessuno: nessuna migrazione, nessun redeploy (skill/autorità/digest non sono importati da `server.mjs` a runtime), `AI_STATE_VERSION` invariato. Il digest resta compatibile — la forma dell'output cambia, non le chiavi.
**Status.** applied. `ARCH-008` resta ⏳ non costruito, ma la sua strada è decisa e non è più una domanda aperta.

**Difetto introdotto e catturato rieseguendo, non leggendo.** La prima correzione al digest annidava apici singoli dentro un programma jq già racchiuso fra apici singoli: `sh -n` **accettava** (shell sintatticamente valida, programma sbagliato) e lo script sporcava stderr. Riscritto formattando con `printf` fuori da jq, stderr riverificato vuoto.

**Proposta di miglioramento (dovuta da §67).** `MANIFEST.sha256` copre 5.845 file ma **non** `.claude/` né `CLAUDE10.md`, e **nessuno strumento in `tools/`/`scripts/` lo verifica** — la verifica è manuale. I documenti che governano ogni fase e definiscono cosa è permesso sono quindi gli unici fuori dal controllo di integrità. Proposta: includerli nel manifest e aggiungere `tools/verify-manifest.mjs` che conti le righe OK invece di fidarsi dell'exit code di `sha256sum -c` (che salta le righe malformate ed esce 0). Beneficio: una modifica silenziosa all'autorità diventa rilevabile. Costo: ~1 tool + 1 rigenerazione del manifest. **Registrata, non eseguita** — aggiungere un tool è una decisione di scope (§5 budget skill).

## D-0248 · ARCH-008 — l'isolamento per capacità costruito e misurato, con un pavimento POSIX che `D-0246` non aveva considerato — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** I limiti viaggiano **dentro il capability token, sotto il suo MAC** (`isolation.mjs` + `capability.mjs`, mirror identico in `noesar-capability::canonical_limits` — stessa stringa byte per byte, ordine delle dimensioni come contratto di wire), e li applica un processo figlio a vita breve prima di diventare il comando (`rust/crates/noesar-sandbox`, nuovo binario `noesar-sandbox`). L'isolamento è un **ladder rilevato a runtime**: tier 0 `setrlimit` (con **anche il limite hard abbassato**, così il figlio non può rialzarselo) + `PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS`, tier 1 seccomp, tier 2 Landlock, tier 3 cgroup v2 — livello **dichiarato per installazione**, mai presunto.
**Why.** La domanda di `D-0246` («autorizzare cambi all'host o rimandare?») era **un errore mio**: l'Owner l'ha rifiutata perché NOESAR EVOLUTION si installa su qualunque PC/server/OS e non possiede mai l'host (`CLAUDE10.md` §16, ora legge). Riformulato il problema, la soluzione era a portata di mano e `D-0246` non l'aveva vista: `setrlimit` è per-processo, POSIX, non richiede opzioni di kernel né delega cgroup né privilegi per **abbassare** un limite. Vale esattamente sugli host dove Landlock e cgroup non ci sono — cioè questo, e Windows/macOS/distro minimali/altri NAS.
**Rejected.** (a) Aspettare un host con Landlock: vietato dalla legge di piattaforma e avrebbe lasciato ARCH-008 fermo per sempre su installazioni altrui. (b) Filtro seccomp con `SECCOMP_RET_KILL_PROCESS`: dà all'operatore un segnale e nessuna ragione; scelto `RET_ERRNO`+EPERM, che è una negazione diagnosticabile. (c) Denylist di syscall scritta a numeri: usati i costanti `libc::SYS_*` per architettura — una tabella hardcoded blocca una chiamata diversa da quella che nomina. (d) Allowlist di syscall: non scrivibile per «codice arbitrario» senza sapere quale, e una sbagliata uccide programmi corretti.
**Evidence.** Misurato dal vivo in container usa-e-getta **sotto il profilo di hardening esatto della produzione** (`--read-only --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --memory 8g`): `--detect` → **tier 1 `SECCOMP_FILTER`**, `rlimit=true noNewPrivs=true seccompFilter=true landlock=false cgroupV2Writable=false`, ceiling del container letto da cgroup = **8589934592**. Poi il criterio stesso: figlio a **64 MiB**, `ulimit -v` **letto da dentro il figlio = 65536 KiB mentre il container è unlimited**; 512 MiB **rifiutati**, 16 MiB **riusciti** (limite reale, non sandbox rotta); `ulimit -Sv 500000` dal figlio → **«error setting limit»**; `cpuSeconds=1` su un `while True` → **exit 137**; `ptrace` → **errno 1 EPERM** (18 syscall filtrate); spec oltre il ceiling → rifiutata **nominando `memoryBytes`**. Manomissione provata: alzare `limits.memoryBytes` su un token emesso → **`does not verify`**; rimuovere `limits` → **idem**; token pulito → spende. Suite: Node **1193/1193** (+25), Rust **47 binari 133 passati 0 falliti** (+26), ESLint **241 file 0 errori**, `MANIFEST` **5853/5853**.
**Reversal cost.** Nessuna migrazione, nessun redeploy: il binario non è ancora nell'immagine e nessuna superficie lo invoca. Il MAC dei token **cambia forma** — un token senza limiti firma `none` e resta identico a prima, quindi nulla di esistente si invalida; i token sono comunque in memoria e non sopravvivono a un riavvio.
**Status.** applied, non installato. `ARCH-008` passa da ⏳ a **⚠ parziale**: il meccanismo esiste ed è misurato, **nessuna superficie del prodotto spende ancora un token attraverso il sandbox** — `executor.mjs` rifiuta `EXECUTE` per progetto e cablarlo è la fase successiva.

**Due difetti trovati ESEGUENDO, non leggendo — uno mio, uno preesistente.**
1. *Mio, riparato nella stessa fase*: la prima misura ha **rifiutato una spec valida da 64 MiB contro un container da 8 GiB**. Causa: una sola relazione usata per due domande diverse. `within` (scopo concesso: un campo non impostato è *illimitato*, quindi allarga) è giusta per «il token sta dentro ciò che l'approvazione ha concesso»; è **sbagliata** per il ceiling del container, dove un campo non impostato è **ereditato**, non illimitato — e il container reale dichiara `openFiles=40960`/`processes=127784` che nessuna spec normale nomina. Separate in `within` e `exceeds`, quest'ultima **nomina la dimensione** che sfonda. 9 test nuovi sui due lati.
2. *Preesistente, riparato*: `rust/crates/noesar-supervisor` — il crate che è **PID 1 del container** dal `D-0240` — **non era in `MANIFEST.sha256`**, mentre ogni altro crate di prima parte c'è. `D-0243` ha rigenerato il manifest e dichiarato 5845/5845 senza accorgersene: il componente più privilegiato del prodotto era l'unico fuori dal controllo di integrità. Aggiunto (3 file).

**Regola rivista dentro la fase, non aggirata.** Avevo imposto «un token `EXECUTE` deve portare i propri limiti». Ha rotto **11 test** su due design entrambi corretti: il gate adattatori di `D-0244` concede `EXECUTE` a `local-model-runtime`, e i test di contratto dell'esecutore emettono un token `EXECUTE` **proprio per provare che l'esecutore lo rifiuta**. Nessuno dei due è un difetto. La regola ora si attiva **solo su un'installazione che i limiti li applica davvero** (ceiling configurato): pretendere un limite prima che qualcosa lo applichi avrebbe registrato una cifra che nessun kernel vede — la cerimonia che questo progetto considera peggiore di un'assenza onesta.

**Proposta di miglioramento (dovuta da §67).** `noesar-sandbox` non è ancora nell'immagine OCI né invocato da `executor.mjs`. Il passo che rende ARCH-008 pieno è un **Sandbox Manager** che spenda ogni token `EXECUTE` attraverso questo binario, il che sblocca anche la superficie `EXECUTE` che l'esecutore rifiuta da sempre «perché non c'è una sandbox che contenga un processo» — ora c'è. Beneficio: `CE-003`/`CE-014` guadagnano un punto di applicazione reale e il prodotto può eseguire test in sandbox invece di rifiutarli. Costo: una fase dedicata (portata paragonabile al supervisore di `ARCH-001`). **Registrata, non eseguita.**

## D-0249 · ARCH-008 completed to "mechanism shipped": OCI image + Node runner, deployed live, EXECUTE deliberately left refused — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** Two additions on top of `D-0248`'s binary: (1) `oci/Dockerfile.phase4-sandbox-binary` compiles `noesar-sandbox` and ships it in the production image; (2) `services/reference-control-plane/src/sandbox-runner.mjs`, a tested Node-side caller (`detectSandbox`/`runSandboxed`, `spawn(binary, argv)` never a shell string, matching `local-model-runtime.mjs`'s own convention). Deployed live per `D-0143` (a phase that changes the product installs it in the same phase). **Deliberately not done**: `executor.mjs`'s `EXECUTE` action was NOT wired to this runner.
**Why.** Mid-phase discovery: `EXECUTE`'s "permanently refused" is not an incidental gap — it is asserted **identically on both language sides**, with the exact reason string part of the shared conformance oracle (`conformance/executor-vectors.json`, case `EXEC-007`, `noesar-executor` and `executor.mjs` both quote it verbatim). Reversing it means editing a cross-language security contract that exists specifically to make "arbitrary command execution from an approved plan" impossible. That is a different, larger decision than "wire the sandbox in" and was never named to the Owner — the recorded proposal that was authorised said "cablarlo a executor.mjs" without knowing this collision existed. Proceeding with everything not blocked by it (image inclusion, a real tested runner) and naming the blocked part explicitly is the honest completion of this phase, not a silent scope cut.
**Rejected.** (a) Editing both conformance vectors and both executor implementations to allow `EXECUTE` under a sandboxed token: real work, real security surface, deserves its own phase and explicit sign-off naming `EXECUTE`, not a rider on "ship the binary". (b) Wiring the runner into a NEW endpoint bypassing `executor.mjs` entirely: would create a second, unaudited path to run arbitrary commands — worse than leaving it unwired.
**Evidence.** Image built `--network=none`; binary verified present and running `--detect` **inside the built image itself** before any deploy. Node wrapper: 14 tests against the REAL binary (skips, with a stated reason, on a host with no binary — never a silent pass), including the ceiling-refusal case re-measured **through the Node caller inside a real `--memory 8g` container** (not just the raw binary as in `D-0248`): small command → exit 0; ceiling+1 → refused pre-exec, exit 78; a 512 MiB Node `Buffer.alloc` under a 64 MiB grant → killed, not leaked. Deployed live: stop `-t 60` with `postgres.stopped clean:true`, backup 12.5 MB, §5a respected (older rollback removed, predecessor preserved), config **read back** from the stopped container, `Up (healthy)`, `/livez`+`/readyz` 200, hardening intact, `migrations:16 rls_tables:15` unchanged, image ID of the running container **byte-identical** to the built image, and `docker exec … noesar-sandbox --detect` on the **live production container** confirms `tier:1 SECCOMP_FILTER` with the real 8 GiB ceiling. Node **1207/1207** (1206 pass + 1 honestly-skipped, 0 fail), ESLint **243 file 0 errori**, `verify-source` PASS, `MANIFEST` **5856/5856**.
**Rejected test-shape finding.** The first ceiling-refusal test asserted `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` must be refused — false on the bare host, where `--detect` itself reports `containerCeiling.memoryBytes:null` (no bounded environment, nothing to be wider than). Not a code defect: fixed by having the test read the real detected ceiling and skip with a named reason when none exists, rather than asserting something untrue on this particular host.
**Reversal cost.** None. No migration, `ENTRYPOINT` unchanged, `AI_STATE_VERSION` unchanged. Rollback to `:phase4-arch005-adapter-gate` only removes the unused binary.
**Status.** installed, verified live. `ARCH-008` stays **⚠ parziale** — the mechanism now ships in production and a real caller exists, but the one path that would spend a capability through it (`EXECUTE`) remains refused by design, pending an explicit Owner decision on reversing a stated cross-language security contract.

**Question for the Owner, not decided here.** Should `EXECUTE` ever be grantable through this sandbox? If yes: which surface may request it (today nothing in the product builds an `EXECUTE` step — `workspace-actions.mjs`'s planner never emits one), and both `conformance/executor-vectors.json` and the two `executor`/`noesar-executor` implementations need a coordinated, explicit change, not an incidental one. If no: `noesar-sandbox` remains real, tested, shipped infrastructure with a single honest purpose — proving ARCH-008's isolation criterion is met — and that is a complete, legitimate end state, not a stub.

## D-0250 · EXECUTE becomes a per-installation client decision — `NOESAR_EXECUTE_SANDBOX`, real end to end in JS; Rust mirror SPLIT OUT, not done here — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** One environment variable, `NOESAR_EXECUTE_SANDBOX` (`disabled` default | `enabled`), mirrors `NOESAR_LOCAL_MODEL_RUNTIME`'s own pattern exactly (`execute-sandbox-config.mjs`, `resolveExecuteSandboxConfig`) — `enabled` only when BOTH the operator asked AND the sandbox binary is present and executable, checked once at boot. Wired for real into the live path: `executor.mjs`'s `EXECUTE` action now goes through the SAME token lookup + spend-before-effect discipline every other kind uses, then runs the command via a new synchronous `runSandboxedSync` (`sandbox-runner.mjs`, `spawnSync`) — chosen over the existing async `runSandboxed` specifically to avoid making `execute()` async, which would have rippled into `workspace-actions.mjs`'s `approve()` and `server.mjs`'s route handler for a capability nothing calls in production yet. The live `TokenMinter` now receives a real `ceiling` (`detectSandboxSync`, probed once at boot, only when enabled) — without it D-0248's mint-time EXECUTE-widening check would silently never fire on any installation.
**Why.** Owner instruction, verbatim: *"FAI MODO CHE IL CLIENTE POSSA DECIDERE"*, in response to the question `D-0249` posed (should EXECUTE ever be grantable). The answer is: not mine to decide once, but a per-installation operator setting, defaulting to the safe answer — same reasoning the platform law (`§16`) already applies to host capability, applied here to a product capability.
**Rejected.** (a) Deciding EXECUTE on/off myself, in code, for every installation: exactly the mistake `D-0249` avoided making by not touching `executor.mjs` at all. (b) Making `execute()` async to reuse the already-built async `runSandboxed`: real ripple cost for zero behavioural gain — `execute()`'s own synchronous `readFileSync`/`writeFileSync`/`rmSync` discipline is a stated property ("the token is spent before the effect" is trivially true in sync code), and `spawnSync` gives the identical three-way outcome shape (refused-before-running / ran-and-failed / ran-and-succeeded) without it.
**Evidence.** Default path (no `executeSandbox` argument) is **byte-identical** to before this phase — same `NO_EXECUTION_SURFACE` reason, `EXEC-007` untouched, proven by a new test asserting exact equality. New paths, each with its own test against the REAL binary: config present but `enabled:false` → a distinct, accurate `EXECUTE_DISABLED_BY_OPERATOR` reason (never confused with "no surface exists"); enabled + token with no limits → defensive refusal (`EXECUTE_TOKEN_WITHOUT_LIMITS`) independent of the mint-time gate; enabled + granted + limited → a REAL `/bin/echo` runs through `noesar-sandbox`, `performed:true`, `stdout` captured; a forged token (one MAC bit flipped) → `performed:0`, spend-before-effect holds. `executorStatus()` no longer claims "there is no sandbox here" unconditionally — that stopped being true the moment `D-0248` shipped the binary; it now reports the operator's actual per-installation answer. Node **1220/1220** (1219 pass + 1 honest skip, 0 fail), ESLint **244 files 0 errors**, `verify-source` PASS, `MANIFEST` **5857/5857**.
**Bug found and fixed, unrelated to the main change but real**: `CapabilityLimits` (Rust) had no `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` — a JSON payload carrying `"memoryBytes"` (the exact wire format both `canonicalLimits` in `isolation.mjs` and `parse_limits` in `noesar-sandbox` use) would have silently deserialized to `memory_bytes: None`, no error raised, because serde ignores unknown JSON keys by default. Never exercised until this phase — no prior conformance vector had populated `limits` from real JSON. Fixed; 2 new Rust tests prove the round-trip. Rust **47 binaries, 135 passed, 0 failed** (+2).
**Deliberately NOT done, and this is a scope decision, not an oversight.** The Rust mirror for EXECUTE-enabled behaviour (`noesar-executor` spawning `noesar-sandbox` natively, matching new conformance vectors both sides satisfy) is **not built in this phase**. Reasons stated plainly: (1) this phase was already running well past its declared budget when the JS side completed; (2) `noesar-executor` is not in the live request path — `services/reference-control-plane` is what is actually installed and serves every request, so the client's decision is real and complete where it matters operationally; (3) adding a NEW conformance vector for functionality only one side implements would be worse than not adding one — the whole reason the shared oracle exists (`F4-014`) is to stop exactly that kind of one-sided claim. `conformance/executor-vectors.json` is untouched by this phase; `EXEC-007` and every existing vector still passes on both sides, unchanged.
**Reversal cost.** None. `NOESAR_EXECUTE_SANDBOX` defaults to `disabled` — today's behaviour is unchanged on every existing installation unless an operator explicitly opts in.
**Status.** installed (source), not yet deployed live — see next action. `ARCH-008`'s remaining gap narrows to exactly one thing: the Rust mirror, named and scoped, not hidden.

**Proposta di miglioramento (dovuta da §67).** Wiring the planner (`workspace-actions.mjs`'s `run.files.map(...)`) to ever emit an `EXECUTE` action is a SEPARATE decision from this one — today, even with `NOESAR_EXECUTE_SANDBOX=enabled`, nothing in the product requests it, so the mechanism is real but dormant everywhere until a plan-authoring surface exists that can ask for it. That surface (what would legitimately need to run a command — tests-in-sandbox is the most obvious candidate, since `CE-020`-adjacent test execution is exactly what `execute()`'s own `tests` parameter already threads through unused) is future work, named not built.

## D-0251 · D-0250 deployato dal vivo — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** `noesar-evolution:phase4-execute-client-decision` in produzione. Nessun rebuild Rust (il fix `rename_all` non è mai compilato nell'immagine). `NOESAR_EXECUTE_SANDBOX=disabled` impostato esplicitamente, stessa visibilità di `NOESAR_LOCAL_MODEL_RUNTIME=disabled`.
**Why.** `D-0250` era fermato per budget di fase, non per un blocco — il deploy è la sequenza già provata di `D-0248`/`D-0249`, a basso rischio dato default `disabled`.
**Rejected.** Nessuna alternativa: il deploy era l'unico passo mancante dichiarato in chiusura.
**Evidence.** Stop pulito (`postgres.stopped clean:true`), backup 12,5 MB, §5a rispettato, config riletta, `Up (healthy)`, `/livez`+`/readyz` 200, hardening intatto, `migrations:16 rls_tables:15` invariate, byte immagine identici. **`docker exec` sul container vivo**, ambiente reale: `resolveExecuteSandboxConfig` → `{enabled:false, requested:false}` — la decisione del cliente, provata dal processo in esecuzione, non assunta.

## D-0252 · ARCH-005 — the "six adapters don't exist" statement audited individually; three get honest empty manifests, three get named reasons for having none — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** `03_ARCHITETTURA.md §4` names seven contracts; `D-0244` gated the one that exists with a privileged operation (`local-model-runtime.launch()`) and left the other six as one undifferentiated "not yet built." That statement conflated two different facts and this phase separates them by reading the actual code, not the doc. Result: `hardware.mjs` (HardwareProbeAdapter), `sector-modules.mjs` (IndustryModuleProvider) and `compliance-packs.mjs` (CompliancePackProvider) are real, shipped, first-party code — but each exposes only read/validate operations (no install, no write, no spawn, no network egress), so there is no privileged operation to self-grant. They now have explicit manifest entries in `ADAPTER_MANIFESTS` with `operations: []`, so `GET /api/v1/adapters` states this as a fact instead of omitting them, which read as "not considered." `VectorStoreAdapter`, `ObjectStoreAdapter` and `HostBridgeAdapter` get no entry at all, each for a distinct, named reason (see below) — adding a manifest for something with no implementation would be inventing a security boundary around nothing.
**Why.** Rule 38/40 (never fabricate state) cuts both ways: it forbids claiming something is gated when it isn't, and it equally forbids leaving a claim ("six adapters don't exist") standing when it's imprecise enough to hide that most of the underlying capability already exists and was never actually at risk. `[[feedback_a_predicate_is_not_audited_by_the_law_that_uses_it]]` and `[[feedback_confirm_function_not_just_form_before_building]]` both apply directly: gating an operation that isn't implemented is form without function.
**Rejected.** (a) Writing manifest stubs for all six with `operations: []` uniformly — false for `VectorStoreAdapter` (postgres-repository.mjs is real, privileged, and would deserve a manifest the moment it becomes a pluggable surface; marking it "no privileged operation" would be wrong, not just incomplete) and for `ObjectStoreAdapter`/`HostBridgeAdapter` for their own distinct reasons — see manifest-adjacent comment in `adapter-capability.mjs`. (b) Building a real `VectorStoreAdapter`/`ObjectStoreAdapter` plugin boundary this phase: `VectorStoreAdapter` has no second implementation to protect against (ARCH-005's own premise doesn't apply yet) and `ObjectStoreAdapter` (content-addressed, encrypted objects) is a missing product feature, not a gating gap — building one to satisfy a capability-token audit would be scope creep in the other direction, inventing a subsystem nobody asked for to make a checklist row green.
**Evidence.** `hardware.mjs` exports exactly `discoverHardware()`/`recommendRuntime()`, both read-only (confirmed by reading the file, not assumed). `sector-modules.mjs`/`compliance-packs.mjs` routes in `server.mjs` are `GET .../[list]` and `POST .../validate` only (grepped every route referencing both modules) — `validate` is a dry run against an in-memory candidate, never persists. `store.mjs` (the only object-shaped store in the tree) is a 22-line plain JSON key-value file, not content-addressed or encrypted. `postgres-repository.mjs` is imported directly by `server.mjs` with one implementation, behind RBAC + Postgres RLS, not behind any adapter-registration mechanism. New tests: manifest now lists four adapters (`adapter-capability.test.mjs`), any operation against the three empty ones is refused `OUT_OF_SCOPE` (12 assertions), `vector-store`/`object-store`/`host-bridge` remain `UNKNOWN_ADAPTER`. `permission-surface.test.mjs`'s existing assertion (`adapterCapabilityList` flattens to exactly one resource/operation pair) still holds unchanged — empty-operations manifests contribute nothing to that list, proving the new entries widen no authority. Node **1222 tests, 1221 pass, 1 honest skip, 0 fail** (+2 net over `D-0251`'s 1220/1220). ESLint **244 files, 0 errors**.
**Reversal cost.** None. No runtime authorization behaviour changes for any existing gated path — `local-model-runtime`'s manifest is byte-identical. The only observable difference is `GET /api/v1/adapters`'s response gaining three keys with empty `operations` arrays.
**Status.** installed and deployed live (see installation ledger). `03_ARCHITETTURA.md`'s `ARCH-005` row rewritten to the precise remaining gap: `VectorStoreAdapter` has no pluggable surface yet, `ObjectStoreAdapter` doesn't exist as a capability yet, `HostBridgeAdapter` is already covered under two other names. Not reopened here: `F4-010` (local-model-runtime `attach()` endpoint hostname-only validation) — tracked separately, deliberately not folded into this phase's claim.

**Proposta di miglioramento (dovuta da §67).** The real remaining ARCH-005 gap is `local-model-runtime.attach()`'s destination validation (`F4-010`) — hostname-string checking, not address-reached checking. A Network Egress Broker (named in the adapter's own code comment as the missing piece) would let `attach()`'s capability grant carry an allow-listed endpoint instead of trusting whatever `configure()` last set. Not built here: `F4-010` is already tracked as accepted-low-severity requiring `provider.manage`/`agent.manage` to exploit, and building a broker to close one low-severity finding is a phase of its own, not a rider on this one.

## D-0253 · ARCH-008 — the Rust mirror of EXECUTE built for real: `noesar-executor` spawns `noesar-sandbox` natively, end to end, proven against the real binary — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** `noesar-executor`'s `execute()` gains a 9th parameter, `execute_sandbox: Option<&ExecuteSandboxConfig>`, mirroring `executor.mjs`'s `executeSandbox` argument exactly: no config → `NO_EXECUTION_SURFACE` (byte-identical to before this phase, `EXEC-007` untouched); a config saying `enabled:false` → the distinct `EXECUTE_DISABLED_BY_OPERATOR`; enabled → the same token-found/spent-before-effect/containment discipline every other action kind already used, then — new — a real `IsolationLimits`-carrying token spends into `run_sandboxed()` (new, ~150 lines), which spawns `noesar-sandbox --spec <tmpfile> -- <command> [args]` via `std::process::Command`, drains stdout/stderr on their own threads (a pipe fills its OS buffer and deadlocks a process blocked on `wait()` otherwise), polls `try_wait()` against a 30s deadline, and distinguishes the identical three outcomes `runSandboxedSync` does: refused-before-running (`EX_CONFIG=78`), ran-and-failed, ran-and-succeeded — down to splitting the sandbox's own JSON report line from the command's real stderr the same way. `Action::Execute` gained a `path` field it never had (the confinement working directory, distinct from `command` — JS already had this, `noesar-executor`'s enum simply lacked the slot) and `ActionOutcome` gained `exit_code`/`stdout`/`stderr`.
**Why.** Named explicitly as the one remaining gap by `D-0250`'s own "Deliberately NOT done" section: building the JS side alone and leaving the Rust reference crate refusing forever would have been the exact one-sided claim `F4-014`'s shared oracle exists to prevent — a mechanism only one language could prove, in a project whose own architecture doc (`03_ARCHITETTURA.md §6`) commits Rust to "ciò che confina."
**Rejected.** (a) Calling `noesar_sandbox::apply()` directly from `noesar-executor`'s own process instead of spawning the `noesar-sandbox` binary: `apply()` narrows the CALLING process permanently (rlimits, seccomp, `no_new_privs` do not un-apply) — correct for `noesar-sandbox`'s own `main.rs`, which immediately `execvp`s away, wrong for `noesar-executor`, which must stay usable for the next action in the same `execute()` call. The whole reason `noesar-sandbox` is a separate short-lived binary (its own doc comment: "a seccomp filter... installed in that process would narrow it permanently") applies to the Rust caller exactly as it does to the JS one. (b) A JSON crate in `run_sandboxed`'s report parser: `noesar-sandbox`'s own `main.rs` already rejected a JSON dependency for the same six-integer spec format with the same reasoning; the caller-side report reader is smaller still (one string field) and inherits the same posture, declared in its own doc comment as "not a general JSON parser."
**Evidence.** Compiles clean (`cargo check --tests`, 0 errors, the two `unused mut` warnings I introduced fixed, the one pre-existing `ShadowLimits`-only-used-in-tests warning left — present before this phase, unrelated to it). `noesar-executor`: 14 lib tests (2 new: `execute_disabled_by_operator_is_a_different_reason_than_no_surface_at_all`, `execute_enabled_but_the_token_carries_no_limits_is_refused_without_spawning_anything`, neither spawns a process), 1 conformance test now checking **12** vectors (`EXEC-011`/`EXEC-012` new, portable, zero-process — the two decision branches D-0250 added, satisfied on both sides), 3 new binary-gated live tests (`tests/sandbox_live.rs`, mirroring `sandbox-runner.test.mjs`'s own `HAVE_BINARY`-skip-with-reason pattern rather than `conformance/executor-vectors.json`, deliberately — a vector spawning a real process is only meaningful on a host where the binary is built, and `D-0250`'s own reasoning against a one-sided vector applies just as much to a not-portable one): a real `/bin/echo` runs through a real `noesar-sandbox` child (`exitCode:0`, `stdout:"ran for real\n"`), a real `/bin/false` is `performed:true, exitCode:1` (ran and failed on its own, not refused), a real 512 MiB allocation attempt under a 64 MiB grant fails (`exitCode != 0`) using the exact values and command shape already proven in `sandbox-runner.test.mjs`'s "THE MEASURED CRITERION" test, not reinvented. Full Rust workspace: **140 tests passed, 0 failed** (up from `D-0250`'s 135 — the +5 is exactly this phase's new tests). Node: **1223 pass, 1 honest skip, 0 fail** (unchanged skip reason, pre-existing). ESLint **244 files, 0 errors**.
**Two real findings, named and deliberately not fixed here.** (1) `noesar-capability`'s Rust `TokenMinter` has **no `ceiling` concept at all** — `D-0248` added a mint-time EXECUTE-widening check to the JS minter only (`capability.mjs`'s `#ceiling`/`exceedsCeiling`); the Rust `mint()` has never had an equivalent. Zero live exploitability: `noesar-executor` is not compiled into any shipped image, confirmed by grepping every other crate's `Cargo.toml` for a dependency on it (none), same reasoning `D-0250` used to defer this whole phase. Registered for whoever next touches `noesar-capability`. (2) `Expectation::try_new` refuses all-three-arguments-empty in Rust; the equivalent JS test (`executor.test.mjs`'s two EXECUTE tests) passes an all-empty literal and JS never gates the shape at all — found writing `sandbox_live.rs`'s own expectation argument, worked around there with a real-but-untouched placeholder path, not chased further (a validation-strictness asymmetry, not a security gap either language's tests currently depend on).
**Reversal cost.** None on the live product: `noesar-executor` is not part of any shipped image, and the two comment-only edits to `executor.mjs`/`sandbox-runner.mjs` (removing the now-doubly-stale "EXECUTE is permanently refused on both language sides" claim `D-0250` had already made half-wrong) change no runtime behaviour.
**Status.** ARCH-008 fully closed: mechanism built, measured, and now spent by EXECUTE on **both** language sides, real process, real kernel-enforced limits, real conformance vectors. `F4-014`'s shared oracle now covers the decision logic on both sides for the enabled path too, not only the always-refused one. Comment fixes deployed live (see installation ledger); the Rust crate itself needs no deployment, it ships nowhere.

## D-0254 · Acceptance-matrix cleanup: `ARCH-001`'s row had been stuck at `D-0240`'s partial state since `D-0242` closed it — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** Reviewed `03_ARCHITETTURA.md §10` for rows a later decision closed without the row being updated (the exact pattern `F4W-011`/`F4W-012` named for the V4 master and `D-0219` fixed there). Found one: `ARCH-001` still read "codev resta assente come terzo figlio" citing only `D-0240`, while `D-0242` (same day, later) made `codev` a real third OS peer via a byte-transparent relay (`bin/codev-child.mjs`) — confirmed by re-reading `D-0242`'s own text, not assumed. Row corrected to `✅ COMPLETO`.
**Why.** Rule 43 (a doc describing behaviour the code does not have is a defect of the same severity as a code bug) cuts the other way too: a doc describing behaviour **worse** than what the code has is equally a defect — it hides completed work and could cause it to be redone.
**Rejected.** A full line-by-line re-audit of every ARCH/INST/SESS/CUBE/CE/UI row against every decision since — genuinely valuable but out of proportion for the tail end of this phase; `ARCH-002` through `ARCH-008` were spot-checked (each cites its own most recent decision correctly) but `INST-001..010`/`SESS-001..003`/`CUBE-001..009` were not re-walked row by row. Named as unfinished, not claimed complete.
**Evidence.** `D-0242`'s text re-read in full; `ARCH-001`'s corrected row names the actual mechanism (relay, not a second engine) and the actual image tag. No code changed, no test suite affected — doc-only, `MANIFEST.sha256` hash for `03_ARCHITETTURA.md` updated, not deployed (the row text is not shipped in any image).
**Reversal cost.** None.
**Status.** `ARCH-001` closed correctly. A full acceptance-matrix re-walk (`INST`/`SESS`/`CUBE`) remains open, named for a future phase rather than rushed here.

## D-0255 · SESS-001 — the Session Proof assembler, wired to a real plan()→approve() run — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** New `session-proof.mjs`: pure `assembleSessionProof({run, events})` builds the ten fields of `01_VISIONE_E_POSIZIONE.md` from real sources on `WorkspaceActionOrchestrator`'s run object and `EventLedger.correlation()` — no field is invented. `GET /api/v1/workspace-actions/:id/session-proof` serves it, same trust level as the existing `GET :id`. Three small honest gaps this exposed were fixed, not routed around: `run.hypotheses`/raw `request` were never stored (added to `plan()`); a refused mint left no event (added `capability.denied`, recorded before the throw); egress was never sampled per-run (`privacyStateFor` injected, sampled at `plan()` and `approve()`, `null` when unwired — reported as absent, not fabricated). `provenienza` reports every source `UNTRACKED` (CUBE-001..009 does not exist); `fixture` declares `replayable:'DECISION_LAYER_ONLY'` (SESS-002 does not exist).
**Why.** SESS-001 is Critical severity and its own acceptance test requires presence **and source** of all ten fields on a real session — assembling from placeholders would pass the test and fail the point.
**Rejected.** Cryptographically signing the package now: a signature over a proof nothing can yet re-derive (SESS-002) is decoration, named in the module comment rather than built.
**Evidence.** `node --test` on the new file: 6/6. Full suite: 1229/1230 (1 pre-existing honest skip), up from 1223 — no regressions. ESLint 246 files, 0 errors. `auth-http-smoke`/`http-smoke` PASS. `scripts/test.sh` 10/10. Browser E2E 327/327, accessibility 27/27, seeded-defect 19/19. `MANIFEST.sha256` 5861/5861. Deployed live (`:phase4-sess001-session-proof`) — `/livez`/`/readyz`/`/healthz` 200/200/200, hardening intact, unauthenticated `GET .../session-proof` answers 401 (route reaches the auth gate). Full deploy narrative, including two self-caused mistakes disclosed rather than smoothed over, in `docs/INSTALLATION_LEDGER.md`.
**Reversal cost.** None: additive route + additive run fields; no existing field removed or renamed.
**Status.** SESS-001 built, verified and deployed live — matrix row updated. SESS-002 (replay engine) and SESS-003 (policy-regression replay) remain unbuilt, next in Block B.
