## D-0257 · A real, already-pushed secret leak found by `tools/run-secret-scan.sh` — flagged for the Owner, not fixed here — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** Ran the real gitleaks scan before pushing this phase's commit (established practice, not a new tier). It found **2 findings, neither from this phase**: `NOESAR_RUST_REASONING_TOKEN` (the live reasoning-router auth secret, `ea38e4f9...`, still active on the running container right now) sits in cleartext inside two committed files — `EVIDENCE/live_config_pre_arch005_manifest_precision_deploy_20260730T111600Z.json` (commit `3bcc9b0`) and `EVIDENCE/live_config_pre_arch008_execute_rust_mirror_deploy_20260730T114253Z.json` (commit `1c31f66`) — full raw `docker inspect .Config.Env` dumps, never redacted. Both commits are **already on `origin/main`** (private repo, but pushed).
**Why.** `B-002` recorded "neither gitleaks nor trufflehog is installed" as the reason no real scan ran — false as stated: `tools/run-secret-scan.sh` (built specifically to close `B-002`'s substance) runs gitleaks from its own disposable, pinned image and needs nothing installed. It had apparently never been run before a push, or its output was not read.
**Rejected.** Rotating `NOESAR_RUST_REASONING_TOKEN` or rewriting git history myself: both are consequential (a live credential change, a force-push that rewrites already-pushed history) and CLAUDE10.md requires the Owner's authorisation for exactly this class of action — flagged instead of acted on.
**Evidence.** `docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/repo zricethezav/gitleaks:latest detect --source /repo --config /repo/.gitleaks.toml -v`: 2 findings, `RuleID: generic-api-key`, both in `EVIDENCE/*.json`, fingerprints and commits recorded above.
**Reversal cost.** N/A — nothing changed. The exposure itself has a cost: anyone with read access to the private repo (or a future publication) can read this token's live value.
**Status.** **Not fixed — Owner decision needed**: (a) rotate `NOESAR_RUST_REASONING_TOKEN` on the live container, (b) decide whether to purge the two commits from history (destructive, changes hashes) or accept the exposure inside a private repo, (c) stop `EVIDENCE/*.json` from ever holding a raw env dump again (redact secrets before writing evidence — a process fix for whichever future phase writes the next one). This phase's own commit does not touch `EVIDENCE/` and does not add to this finding.

## D-0258 · `B-011` history rewritten on Owner's explicit authorisation — token deliberately NOT rotated yet — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** Owner, verbatim: *"non ruotare ancora, l'importante è che non resti in chiaro. poi quando è pronto il progetto la cambio, sì riscrivi git"*. Backed up the full repo (`git bundle create BACKUPS/pre_history_rewrite_20260730T131500Z.bundle --all`, verified), confirmed the secret string appeared in exactly 2 files across all 215 commits (`git rev-list --all` grep), then `git filter-branch --tree-filter` replaced `NOESAR_RUST_REASONING_TOKEN`'s value with `REDACTED_D-0257_ROTATE_BEFORE_REUSE` in both files, everywhere in history. `refs/original/*` removed, reflog expired, `git gc --prune=now --aggressive` run — 0 unreachable objects left holding the old blob. Force-pushed (`git ls-remote` confirmed `origin/main` unchanged since this session's own last push, so nothing else was overwritten).
**Why.** The Owner's own words: the secret must not remain readable, and rotation is a separate, later decision — not a reason to delay removing it from history now.
**Rejected.** `--force-with-lease`: rejected as stale because `filter-branch --all` also rewrote the local `refs/remotes/origin/main` tracking ref, invalidating the lease's own comparison basis. Verified the true remote state with `git ls-remote` instead of blindly forcing.
**Evidence.** Fresh clone of `origin/main` from GitHub (`/tmp/_verify_remote_clean`, removed after use): `git rev-list --all` grepped for the raw token value across every commit — zero matches. `tools/run-secret-scan.sh`'s own gitleaks re-run: 2 findings remain, both on the **placeholder string itself** (`REDACTED_D-0257...` trips the same entropy-shaped `generic-api-key` rule) — confirmed by reading the content directly, not a live secret.
**Reversal cost.** The two original commits (`3bcc9b0`, `1c31f66`) no longer exist under those hashes; every commit from them onward has a new hash. The pre-rewrite state is fully recoverable from `BACKUPS/pre_history_rewrite_20260730T131500Z.bundle` (gitignored, not pushed) if ever needed.
**Status.** History cleaned and pushed. `NOESAR_RUST_REASONING_TOKEN`'s live value is now `[UNVERIFIED as still-current]` only in the running container's own environment and `atomd`'s config — nowhere in git. Rotation deliberately deferred to the Owner, at project completion, per their own instruction. `B-011` updated: `blocks_next_phase:false`, cleartext-in-git closed, rotation left open on purpose.

## D-0259 · SESS-002 + SESS-003 — the replay engine, both halves — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** Extracted `#runDecisionLayer` (interpret→hypothesize→buildPlan→constrain→classify→confidence→expect) out of `plan()` so it is called, not re-implemented, by two new operations. `replay(runId)` (SESS-002): if every decision surface answered locally, recompute with a fresh provider and structurally compare (`compareDecisions`, `session-replay.mjs`) against what the run recorded; if any decision surface was external, resubmit the `fixturePack` captured at `plan()` time (new: `runId` now threads as `ReasoningRouter`'s `sessionId`, and `provider.fixtures(runId)` is called best-effort right after `expect()`) to that SAME provider's own `/v1/replay` — an ATOM extension already proven faithful by `tools/measure-replay-fidelity.mjs` (D-0227) — and report its verdict as-is, never regenerated by a different provider. `replayHistoricalFixture()` (SESS-003): the same `#runDecisionLayer`, run against an externally-supplied fixture with NO in-memory run behind it, comparing the recomputed refusal/risk to a caller-supplied historical outcome (`comparePolicyOutcome`) — a `CONSTRAINED_AWAY` on replay is reported as drift, not thrown as an error. Two routes: `POST /api/v1/workspace-actions/:id/replay`, `POST /api/v1/session-proof/replay` — both `workspace.read` + CSRF, same trust level as `simulate` (no token minted, nothing executed).
**Why.** Both were the named next step after `D-0255`. `SESS-002`'s own fixture already declared `DECISION_LAYER_ONLY`/no external capture as an honest gap — this phase closes it for real rather than leaving the declaration as the permanent answer.
**Rejected.** A second comparison engine that re-derives "same decision" from scratch: `compareDecisions` is deliberately a dumb structural diff over the SAME fields `#runDecisionLayer` produces — the semantics live in exactly one place, called twice. Also rejected: reading `process.env` directly in `replay()`'s external path — untestable and silently inconsistent with whatever `env` a caller's own `reasoningFor` used; the orchestrator now stores `env` itself (default `process.env`, unchanged in production) and both the default `reasoningFor` and `replay()` read the same one.
**Evidence.** Real bug caught building this and fixed before any test masked it: `usedExternal` (deciding LOCAL vs EXTERNAL_PACK) first checked ANY `atom` provenance entry, which included `fixtures` itself — a run that routed only the capture surface externally (decision fully local) would have wrongly taken the EXTERNAL_PACK path. Fixed with `DECISION_SURFACES` (the six surfaces that actually produce a decision; `fixtures` deliberately excluded), shared by `workspace-actions.mjs` and `session-proof.mjs`'s own `fixtureOf()`, which had the identical bug. 17 new tests (`session-replay.test.mjs`): pure comparators, injectable `callAtomReplay` (success/refused/unreachable), a real reference-provider run replaying faithful, a **provoked divergence** (a provider that answers differently on the second call — proves the detector fires, not just passes), unknown-runId refusal, a full `/v1/fixtures`→`/v1/replay` round trip through a local HTTP stub, capture-failure declared honestly, and both SESS-003 cases (no drift; current code refusing what history says was permitted). Full suite **1246/1247** (+18, 1 pre-existing honest skip), ESLint **248 files 0 errors**, `scripts/test.sh` **10/10**, seeded-defect **19/19**, `auth-http-smoke`/`http-smoke` PASS, `MANIFEST.sha256` **5863/5863**.
**Reversal cost.** None on the live product's existing behaviour: `plan()`'s own contract (inputs, outputs, refusal kinds) is unchanged — only additive fields (`fixturePack`) and two new read-only routes.
**Status.** SESS-002 and SESS-003 built, tested, matrix rows updated. Block B (SESS-001..003) complete. Next: Block C, `CUBE-001..009` — a whole subsystem, 0/9, not yet scoped into phases.

## D-0260 · Block C's open Owner questions (`14 §7`) — the doc's own proposed defaults adopted, not invented — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** `14_MEMORIA_A_CUBI.md §7` lists five questions the doc's own author left to the Owner, never answered since 26 July. Adopting the doc's own proposed default for each, since each was already argued for, not guessed fresh: (1) PostgreSQL authoritative — **already decided**, `§10`, `B-009`. (2) The nine categories of `§3.2` stand unextended. (3) Promotion: arrival in `*-candidate` is automatic, `project`/`global` requires approval (schema already encodes this via `promotion_state`'s six values; no code enforces the rule yet — a later phase). (4) Retention: a session item never expires on its own. (5) The Corpus cube extends the existing knowledge graph rather than a second document store.
**Why.** `noesar-evolution` skill, "decide technical choices yourself" (the Owner's own standing instruction) — stalling nine open acceptance criteria on five questions whose answers were already written, by the same standard I would apply now, is not caution, it is friction.
**Rejected.** Asking the Owner before writing any schema: the schema in `§9.2` does not actually depend on (3)/(4)/(5) at the DDL level — those are application-layer rules for a later phase. Only (1) was a real schema precondition, and it was already resolved.
**Evidence.** N/A — a documentation decision, not a measurement.
**Reversal cost.** Low for (2)/(3)/(4): a category or a retention rule can be added later (the doc itself says "si estende con una decisione registrata"). (5) has real cost if reversed after Corpus content exists in a specific place — named, not chased further here.
**Status.** Adopted. If the Owner disagrees with any of the five, correcting it now costs one migration; correcting it after C2-C9 are built on top costs a rewrite.

## D-0261 · CUBE fase C1 — the memory-cubes schema, migration `0017`, verified against a real disposable PostgreSQL — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** `database/postgres/0017_memory_cubes.sql`: `embedding_models` (one `is_current` model, partial unique index), `memory_records` (the four-cube ENUM, the immutable signature via `signature_is_immutable()` trigger, the nine closed categories, `derived_must_cite`, `counters_only_for_experience`, RLS via the SAME `can_read_resource`/`can_write_resource` functions every other resource table uses), `memory_vectors` (one row per `(record, model)`, HNSW index), six non-vector catalogue indices. One addition beyond `14 §9.2`'s literal text: a `visibility` column on `memory_records` (the doc's schema omits it; every sibling resource table carries it) — disclosed in the migration's own header comment, not silently added.
**Why.** `CUBE-001/002/005/007` are all schema-provable in isolation — a trigger and three constraints, each with a direct SQL test — before any application code exists to read or write through them. Building the provable half first, separately from the unprovable-without-a-service-layer half (`CUBE-003/006/008/009`), is the same split `SESS-001` made between "assemble the ten fields" and "build the replay engine that uses them."
**Rejected.** Waiting for the JS service layer before writing the migration: the schema is independently testable and independently valuable (it also fixes `CUBE-005`'s underlying defect — `vector_entries`, already live-unreferenced, has never carried a model identity, so two embedding spaces are silently comparable today). Building both at once would have meant a much larger, much less falsifiable phase.
**⚠️ A real architectural tension found building this, not resolved here.** `CUBE-004` (Critical) demands the four cubes be separated "by different tables/types... not even a programming error" can confuse them. The doc's OWN concrete schema in `§9.2` — which this migration implements close to verbatim — puts all four cubes in **one table**, `memory_records`, distinguished only by an ENUM column. A query that forgets `WHERE cube = 'library'` compiles, runs, and silently returns Corpus rows too: exactly the failure mode `CUBE-004` says must be structurally impossible, not merely conventionally avoided. This is a contradiction inside the spec itself, between its stated principle (`§5` point 5, `CUBE-004`) and its own recommended DDL (`§9.2`) — not something I introduced building it. Two real fixes exist and neither is applied yet: (a) four typed, `WITH CHECK OPTION` views over `memory_records`, one per cube, with direct table access revoked from `noesar_app` so every read/write is forced through a view that cannot return or accept the wrong cube; (b) four genuinely separate tables (more faithful to `CUBE-004`'s literal wording, more schema duplication for the columns all four share). **Named for the Owner, not decided by default**: the migration ships with the one-table design because it is what `§9.2` recommends and what `§9.6`'s dependency order requires as a foundation, but `CUBE-004` is NOT satisfied by it as it stands.
**Evidence.** Static: `scripts/test.sh` pg-migrations + pg-contract **PASS** (`tools/verify-postgres-migrations.py`'s hardcoded 16-file expected-list updated to 17, `MIGRATIONS.json` regenerated). **Live, against a real disposable instance** — built `oci/Dockerfile.phase4-cube-c1-schema` (adds `database/postgres/` to the already-tested `:phase4-sess002-003-replay` image, which had never had the migrations directory baked in for a fresh install to apply from — a real gap in how I'd been building images this session, caught here), ran it `--network none` against a scratch workspace, confirmed `migrations:17` in the boot log, then via `psql` over the unix socket: (1) valid `INSERT` succeeds, (2) `UPDATE` changing the signature → rejected by the trigger with the exact old/new values in the error, (3) `UPDATE` on an ordinary field still works, (4) `derived=true` with empty `derived_from` → rejected, (5) a category outside the nine → rejected, (6) a second `is_current=true` model → rejected by the partial unique index, (7) a `memory_vectors` insert against the current model → succeeds, (8) `confirmations` set on a non-`experience` row → rejected. All eight matched the intended behaviour. Container and scratch workspace removed after.
**Reversal cost.** None on the live product: three new tables, zero existing tables altered, zero application code reads or writes them yet.
**Status.** `CUBE-001/002/005(schema)/007` closed and verified live. `CUBE-004` open and flagged — needs the Owner's choice between the two fixes above (or accepting the gap) before `C2` builds application code on top of this table. `CUBE-003/006/008/009` unbuilt, need the service layer. Deployed live (schema-only, additive, safe) — see `docs/INSTALLATION_LEDGER.md`.

## D-0262 · `CUBE-004` closed — typed views over `memory_records`, migration `0018`, plus an independent RESTRICTIVE-policy defect found and fixed in the same pass — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** Asked the Owner which of `D-0261`'s two proposed fixes to build. Answer: typed views + `REVOKE`, not four separate tables. `database/postgres/0018_memory_cube_typed_views.sql`: four views (`library_memories`/`workshop_memories`/`corpus_memories`/`experience_memories`), each `SELECT * FROM memory_records WHERE cube = '<x>' WITH CHECK OPTION`, owned by `noesar_migrator` (not the migration's own superuser connection — see next paragraph), with a per-view `DEFAULT` on the `cube` column so a caller that never mentions it still lands correctly. `noesar_app`'s direct `SELECT`/`INSERT`/`UPDATE` on `memory_records` is revoked; the views are the only path left, and `WITH CHECK OPTION` rejects both an `INSERT` that names the wrong cube and an `UPDATE` that would move a row out of its own cube — structural rejection, not a convention, which is exactly what `CUBE-004`'s acceptance row asks for.
**Why `noesar_migrator` owns the views, not the migration's superuser connection.** PostgreSQL checks a plain view's underlying-table permissions against the VIEW OWNER, not the querying role — the entire point, since it is what lets `noesar_app` keep working after its own direct grant is revoked. But if the owner is a superuser (this migration runs as `noesar_admin`, the cluster superuser), row-level security is bypassed **entirely** for every query through the view — superuser bypass is unconditional and `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` does not override it. That would have turned "typed views" into "read every workspace's memories through a view." `noesar_migrator` (`NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS`, not `memory_records`' actual owner) is fully subject to the table's RLS same as `noesar_app` would have been, so scoping survives the indirection. Verified live, not assumed — see Evidence.
**Why `memory_vectors`' policy is rewritten too.** Its `0017` policy joined `memory_records` inline (`EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM memory_records r WHERE ...)`), an ordinary SQL reference requiring the querying role's own `SELECT` grant on `memory_records`. Revoking `noesar_app`'s grant without touching this would have broken every `memory_vectors` query. Fixed by mirroring `0015`'s own pattern for `is_workspace_member`/`is_project_member` ("a membership lookup made by a policy on a table that itself has RLS would recurse"): two new `SECURITY DEFINER` functions, `can_read_memory_record`/`can_write_memory_record`, restating the exact predicate `memory_records`' own policy uses. `memory_vectors`' policy now calls the function instead of joining a table `noesar_app` can no longer see directly.
**⚠️ A second, independent defect found live-verifying this, not introduced by it.** All three of `0017`'s policies (`memory_records`, `memory_vectors`, `embedding_models`) are declared `AS RESTRICTIVE`, and each is the *only* policy on its table. PostgreSQL combines `RESTRICTIVE` policies with `AND` on top of `PERMISSIVE` ones — a `RESTRICTIVE` policy can only narrow a grant that already exists. With zero `PERMISSIVE` policies present there is nothing to narrow, so access is denied unconditionally, for every role, forever — `memory_records` was never actually writable by `noesar_app` since `0017` was deployed. Reproduced live against the **unmodified** `0017` schema (no `0018` involved, direct grant still present): a `noesar_app` `INSERT` with a real, matching workspace/owner still failed with "new row violates row-level security policy"; adding a trivial `USING (true)` `PERMISSIVE` policy alongside the existing one was enough to let the identical statement through. `0015`'s own two `RESTRICTIVE` policies (`noesar_document_ownership`, `noesar_memory_ownership`) only work because `documents`/`memory_items` already carried a `PERMISSIVE` tenancy policy from `0007` — `0017`'s three tables are new and never had that predecessor; the `RESTRICTIVE` marker reads like it was copied from `0015`'s ownership-policy shape without its prerequisite. Silent since deploy because, per `0017`'s own header, nothing has read or written these tables yet. Cannot fix by editing `0017` — already applied to the live product (`D-0261`) and migrations are immutable once applied (`0008`'s ledger trigger). Fixed inside `0018` instead: each policy is dropped and recreated without the `RESTRICTIVE` marker (`PERMISSIVE`, PostgreSQL's default), the same self-sufficient shape `0015`'s own loop already uses for `vector_entries`/`conversations`/`agents`/`tools`, where `can_read_resource`/`can_write_resource` are the whole rule rather than a narrowing layer on top of an earlier grant that, for these three tables, never existed.
**Rejected.** Four separate tables (the Owner's other option) — not chosen; the Owner's stated reasoning per the question asked was to avoid duplicating the shared columns and keep `0017`'s trigger/constraints/indexes applying uniformly instead of four times over.
**Evidence.** Static: `scripts/test.sh` pg-migrations + pg-contract **PASS** (`tools/verify-postgres-migrations.py`'s expected-list extended to `0018`, `MIGRATIONS.json` regenerated, 18 entries). Full suite: `scripts/test.sh` 10/10 STEP, `npm test` 1246/1247 (1 pre-existing skip, unrelated), `npm run lint` 248 files / 0 errors. **Live, against a real disposable PostgreSQL** (`oci/Dockerfile.phase4-cube-typed-views`, `FROM :phase4-cube-c1-schema`, adds `database/postgres/` + `tools/acceptance/` on top): extended `tools/acceptance/postgres-integration.mjs` (the project's own permanent in-container harness, not a throwaway psql session this time, so `C2`+ inherits durable regression coverage instead of a one-off proof) with `CUBE04-01..08` — direct `SELECT`/`INSERT` on `memory_records` denied; `INSERT` through a view with no `cube` column defaults correctly; `INSERT` through the wrong view with an explicit wrong `cube` value rejected by `CHECK OPTION` ("new row violates check option for view \"workshop_memories\""); the library view never returns a workshop row from the same owner/workspace; `UPDATE` attempting to move a row out of its cube rejected by `CHECK OPTION`, row provably unchanged after; `memory_vectors` still accepts a legitimate index write and still refuses one for another workspace's record (the `SECURITY DEFINER`-function regression test). **57/57 PASS**, zero failures, including all pre-existing `DB-*` checks (no regression). Also confirmed the `RESTRICTIVE`-only defect and its fix empirically in an isolated hypothesis test against the unmodified `0017` schema before writing the final fix (see paragraph above) — a container/scratch workspace, not the live product.
**Deploy.** `docker stop -t 60` → `postgres.stopped clean:true` confirmed in the log → backup `BACKUPS/runtime_pre_cube_typed_views_deploy_20260730T152454Z.tar.gz` (12.7 MB, service stopped) → §5a (older rollback `cube-c1-schema-...T144721Z` removed, predecessor renamed to `.rollback-cube-typed-views-20260730T152454Z`) → new container from the full `docker inspect` `HostConfig`/`Env` JSON, env re-verified comma-separated before use. **Clean on the first attempt**: `Up (healthy)` at 12s, `data-plane.ready migrations:18 rls_tables:18 production_ready:true`, `/livez`/`/readyz`/`/healthz` all 200, hardening intact (`ReadonlyRootfs:true CapDrop:[ALL] Tmpfs:{/run:mode=1777,/tmp}`, `RestartCount:0`). Byte identity of the two changed/new files (`0018_memory_cube_typed_views.sql`, `MIGRATIONS.json`) confirmed via `docker cp` + `diff` against the repository tree. Post-deploy inventory: exactly 2 `noesar-evolution*` containers, `noesar-evolution-net` the only project network.

Predecessor: `noesar-evolution.rollback-cube-typed-views-20260730T152454Z` (`:phase4-cube-c1-schema`). Rollback cost: reintroduces both the `CUBE-004` gap and the `RESTRICTIVE`-only defect (`memory_records`/`memory_vectors`/`embedding_models` become unwritable by `noesar_app` again) — no data loss, since nothing has read or written these tables in application code yet.
**Status.** `CUBE-004` closed and verified live. The `RESTRICTIVE`-only defect (found this phase, not previously tracked under any `CUBE-*`/`F4-*` id) closed and verified live. `CUBE-003/006/008/009` still unbuilt, need the service layer — Block C2 unblocked, no Owner decision pending.

## D-0263 · Block C2-C4 — recall(), extractive compaction, contamination canary, promotion (`CUBE-003`/`CUBE-006`) — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** The service layer over the cube schema, in one phase: `services/reference-control-plane/src/memory-service.mjs` (new) and `memory-compaction.mjs` (new), migration `0019` (a read-only `all_memories` view — `UNION ALL` of the four typed views, so `recall()`'s optional `cube` filter can search everywhere without reopening `CUBE-004`: every row still carries the literal `cube` it came from, nothing here can misreport one), and `approval-queue.mjs` gains a fourth source (`memory-candidate`) so promotion reuses the exact "reads the subsystem that owns it, holds no copy" pattern the other three already use.
**Two architectural gaps found scoping this, resolved without expanding scope.** (1) `B-009`'s "reconciliation" (§9.6 point 1) turned out to be near-vacuous in practice: `memory_items` (0006), `state.memories` (the JSON manual-notes feature), and `noesar_core.conversations`/`conversation_messages` are ALL confirmed empty in production (0 rows each) and the live chat path never reads/writes the Postgres conversation tables at all — there is nothing to migrate FROM. "PostgreSQL is authoritative" is executed by simply never writing new cube memory anywhere else, not by a dual-write migration over data that does not exist. (2) The live product has no multi-workspace concept in its request path at all (`grep workspace_id services/reference-control-plane/src/server.mjs` — zero matches) even though Postgres's RLS is fully multi-tenant. Rather than build workspace management to satisfy a schema `NOT NULL`, one fixed workspace (`CANONICAL_WORKSPACE_ID`, a literal constant) is projected at boot — the identical "projection, not migration" idea `user-directory.mjs` already uses for identity, restated: `ensureWorkspace()` is idempotent, attaches the workspace to whichever projected identity has `role='owner'`, and runs right after the identity projection in the boot sequence for that reason.
**What "the session's events from the ledger" means for compaction, decided not assumed.** `§9.5` step 1 says the source is "the ledger, already append-only and chained." Two ledgers exist; only `EventLedger` (`events.mjs`) is that shape — hash-chained, one `correlationId` per workspace-actions run, exactly what `D-0259`'s replay engine already reads. It is also where this product's actual decisions/facts/defects already live as STRUCTURED, typed event payloads (`workspace_action.planned`'s `goal`, `executor.ran`'s `performed`/`refused`/`ok`, `workspace_action.refused`'s `reason`) rather than prose to be mined — "estrarre prima di generare" (§4.1 rule 1) is satisfied by construction, not by discipline: every candidate is a template filled from an event's own field, never free text a human wrote. `ACTION_RULES` in `memory-compaction.mjs` is a closed table (`workspace_action.planned/approved/rejected`, `capability.denied`, `executor.ran`, `workspace_action.claims_verified/promoted/refused`, `shadow.compared`) — an event whose action is not a key in it produces NO candidate, silently, ever, which is stricter than "discard if untraceable": there is no code path that can emit something for an event this file does not recognise, because emission is table-driven, not inferred. `workspace_action.simulated`/`.restored`/`.replayed`/`capability.minted` are deliberately absent — noise, the way §4.1's own examples name it.
**The contamination canary, made concrete.** `write()` computes a derived record's effective contamination as the WORST of what the caller claims and what its `derivedFrom` sources actually carry — a record cannot claim `verified` while citing something `suspect`/`revoked`; the claim is silently overridden, not merely validated, which is what "resta marcato per sempre, anche dopo la promozione" (§5 point 4) requires: contamination cannot be laundered through one derivation step.
**A real bug found live-verifying the admin-mediated paths, fixed before it shipped.** `listCandidates()`/`promote()` originally queried through `all_memories`/the typed views under an admin (`withAdmin`) connection — reasoned, wrongly, that a superuser connection bypasses RLS regardless of what it queries. PostgreSQL enforces a plain (non-`security_invoker`) view's RLS using the VIEW OWNER's identity, not the connecting role's, for the same reason `D-0262` chose `noesar_migrator` as the view owner in the first place; an admin connection never sets `noesar.actor_id`, so querying THROUGH the view returned zero rows regardless of what actually existed — reproduced live (`listCandidates()` found 0 of a known-existing candidate), fixed by querying `noesar_knowledge.memory_records` directly for these two admin-mediated, already-privileged, `noesar_app`-unreachable methods (`cube` kept as an extra `WHERE` filter on `promote()`, not dropped, so a caller naming the wrong cube for a real signature is refused rather than silently acting on it).
**Rejected.** Promotion via the RLS-scoped path `write()` uses: a candidate is written `visibility:'private'` (only its own actor can see it while undecided) and the person deciding is very often not that actor (the Owner approving something a background compaction wrote) — `can_write_resource`'s owner-only check would refuse the operation `promote()` exists to perform. Gating the shared `/api/v1/approvals/:id/decision` route's permission per-item-kind (so `memory.manage` alone could decide a memory candidate): the route currently gates ALL four kinds with one blanket `agent.manage` check; loosening that for one kind risks the other three and was not asked for — memory promotion joins the existing admin/operator tier instead, consistent with treating "make a record authoritative for the whole project/workspace" as at least as privileged as an agent-step approval.
**Evidence.** Unit: `memory-service.test.mjs` (22 tests) + `memory-compaction.test.mjs` (5 tests) with a `FakeClient` mock (same pattern `postgres-repository.test.mjs` already uses) — validation, SQL shape, the canary's severity math, promotion transitions, the `cube`-mismatch refusal. `npm test` **1271/1272** (1 pre-existing unrelated skip, no regressions — `approval-queue.test.mjs`'s 10 HTTP-level tests, now exercising `list()`/`counts()` as async, still pass unchanged). `npm run lint` 253 files / 0 errors. **Live, against a real disposable PostgreSQL** (new permanent harness `tools/acceptance/memory-integration.mjs`, `oci/Dockerfile.phase4-memory-application-layer`): `ensureWorkspace()` before/after an owner exists and idempotently a third time; `write()` through real views with real RLS; the derived-without-`derivedFrom` refusal; the contamination canary escalating a real `verified`-claiming write to `suspect` because it cited a real `suspect` row; `recall()` returning real cross-cube results via `all_memories`, honest `coverage.vectorIndexComplete:false` with no embedding model configured, a cube-scoped recall never crossing cubes, and an explicit `not_found` for a query with zero matches; `listCandidates()`/`promote()` — the bug reproduced BEFORE the fix (0 candidates found despite one existing), then **24/24 PASS** after; `compactRun()` against a real three-event `EventLedger` writing 2 real rows and skipping 1 unrecognised event, verified in the database by `provenance->>'runId'`, not by trusting the return value.
**Deploy.** `docker stop -t 60` → `postgres.stopped clean:true` → backup `BACKUPS/runtime_pre_memory_application_layer_deploy_20260730T165253Z.tar.gz` (12.8 MB) → §5a (older rollback `cube-typed-views-...T152454Z` removed, predecessor renamed to `.rollback-memory-application-layer-20260730T165253Z`) → new container from the full `docker inspect` JSON. **Clean on the first attempt**: `Up (healthy)` at 12s, `data-plane.ready migrations:19 rls_tables:18`, `data-plane.workspace-projected ensured:true` with the real owner's id in the boot log, `/livez`/`/readyz` 200/200, hardening intact, `RestartCount:0`. Byte identity of all four changed/new files confirmed via `docker cp` + `diff`. Post-deploy inventory: exactly 2 `noesar-evolution*` containers.
**Reversal cost.** None on live data: `all_memories` is a new read-only view: `memory-service.mjs`/`memory-compaction.mjs` are new files nothing else calls except the four new integration points in `server.mjs`/`approval-queue.mjs`, and no application code wrote through them before this phase.
**Status.** `CUBE-003` closed and verified live (fail-closed compaction, provably discards the unrecognised-event case). `CUBE-006` closed and verified live (items/coverage/not_found, all three properties). Contamination canary and promotion approval built and verified live (not a separate `CUBE-*` id — part of `§4`/`§9.5` step 8's "canary di contaminazione e pipeline di promozione"). Remaining in Block C: `CUBE-008` (embedding model swap, measured end-to-end) and `CUBE-009` (the WebUI surface) — next.

## D-0264 · Block C5 — the embedding model swap procedure (`CUBE-008`) — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** `services/reference-control-plane/src/memory-model-swap.mjs` (new): `ModelSwapService` implements `§9.3`'s four steps as four methods — `registerModel()` (inserts `is_current:false`), `backfillBatch()` (finds up to `batchSize` records the model has not indexed yet via `NOT EXISTS` against `memory_vectors`, embeds and inserts one at a time — a crash mid-batch loses at most the in-flight record, not the whole procedure), `activate()` (refuses below 100% coverage with a `409`, otherwise flips `is_current` old→false/new→true inside one `BEGIN`/`COMMIT` so `recall()` never observes zero or two current models), `purgeSuperseded()` (refuses to delete the CURRENT model's index, only ever a model already superseded by `activate()`).
**No real embedding model is wired into this product** — verified the same way `recall()`'s own header already establishes (grepped the source, no TEI/model client exists anywhere in `reference-control-plane`). `embed` is an INJECTED function parameter, never a default this file supplies: the swap MECHANISM (atomicity, no downtime, no data loss) is buildable and testable today without fabricating a semantic-search capability that does not exist. `CUBE-008`'s own criterion is about the mechanism, not about real semantic vectors — "misurata end-to-end su un corpus di prova" is satisfied by a real corpus of real `memory_records` rows going through the real procedure, independent of where the embedding numbers come from.
**Admin-mediated throughout, same reasoning as `D-0263`'s `listCandidates()`/`promote()` fix**: this reads/writes `memory_vectors`/`embedding_models` system-wide, across every workspace and cube — not a `noesar_app`-scoped action. Reading `memory_records` directly (not through the four typed cube views) does not reopen `CUBE-004`: the index rows this writes key only on `(record_id, model_id)` and never carry or interpret a `cube` value.
**A real bug found live-verifying this, fixed before it shipped.** `purgeSuperseded()` reported `deleted:0` against a verified real 7-row corpus. Root cause: this project's hand-rolled PostgreSQL client (`pg-client.mjs`) computes a query's `rowCount` from the number of rows in the RETURNED result set, not from PostgreSQL's own `CommandComplete` tag — a `DELETE` with no `RETURNING` clause returns zero rows by definition regardless of how many it actually deleted, so `rowCount` was always 0. The project's own existing convention (`postgres-integration.mjs`'s `DB-17`, `DELETE ... RETURNING id`) already establishes the fix for exactly this reason; applied the same way here (`DELETE ... RETURNING record_id`).
**Rejected.** Building or wiring a real embedding model to make this "more end-to-end": out of scope for finishing Block C and a materially larger undertaking (a whole model-serving integration this product has never had) — the swap mechanism's correctness does not depend on it, and claiming otherwise would be exactly the kind of unmeasured claim this project's own discipline refuses to make.
**Evidence.** Unit: `memory-model-swap.test.mjs` (11 tests, `FakeAdmin` mock) — `is_current` never inserted true, coverage math, the atomic `BEGIN`/`is_current=false`/`is_current=true`/`COMMIT` sequence, rollback on a simulated mid-transaction failure, both refusal paths (`activate()` below 100%, `purgeSuperseded()` on the current model), 503 with no data plane. `npm test` **1284/1285** (1 pre-existing unrelated skip). `npm run lint` 255 files / 0 errors. **Live, against a real disposable PostgreSQL** (`tools/acceptance/memory-integration.mjs` extended with `MEM-25..36`): registered a model against the real 7-row corpus left by `D-0263`'s own checks, backfilled it fully in one batch, confirmed `activate()` refuses an unbackfilled second model (`0/7`), activated the first, confirmed exactly one `is_current` row, confirmed `recall()` itself flips from the honest `vectorIndexComplete:false` (`D-0263`, `MEM-12`) to `true` with the real model name — a second model then supersedes the first (register→backfill→activate again), `purgeSuperseded()` reproduced the bug BEFORE the fix (`deleted:0` against a known 7), then **35/35 PASS** after, including `memory_records` provably untouched (still 7) and `recall()` still complete under the new model.
**Deploy.** `docker stop -t 60` → `postgres.stopped clean:true` → backup `BACKUPS/runtime_pre_memory_model_swap_deploy_20260730T170329Z.tar.gz` (12.9 MB) → §5a (older rollback `memory-application-layer-...T165253Z` removed, predecessor renamed to `.rollback-memory-model-swap-20260730T170329Z`) → new container from the full `docker inspect` JSON. **Clean on the first attempt**: `Up (healthy)` at 12s, `data-plane.ready migrations:19 rls_tables:18`, `data-plane.workspace-projected ensured:true`, `/livez`/`/readyz` 200/200, hardening intact, `RestartCount:0`. Byte identity of the two changed/new files confirmed via `docker cp` + `diff`. Post-deploy inventory: exactly 2 `noesar-evolution*` containers.
**Reversal cost.** None on live data: `memory-model-swap.mjs` is a new file nothing else calls; no model has been registered or activated on the live product (the live corpus's `embedding_models` table remains empty in production — this phase only proves the mechanism against a disposable instance).
**Status.** `CUBE-008` closed and verified live. Remaining in Block C: `CUBE-009` (the WebUI `Memoria` destination) — the last item.

## D-0265 · Block C6 — the Memory WebUI destination, and Block C is now complete (`CUBE-009`) — 2026-07-30
**Decision.** A thirteenth sidebar destination, "Memory" (`apps/webui-static/index.html`/`app.js`), backed entirely by what `D-0263`/`D-0264` already built: `GET /api/v1/memory/recall` for search AND browse (§11's two gestures collapse into one call — an empty query is a browse, a filled one is a search), the existing four-source `ApprovalQueue` for the third (Keep/Discard on anything new). No new backend route beyond `recall()` — approving/discarding a memory candidate reconstructs the exact `memory-candidate:${cube}:${signature}` id `D-0263` already defined and posts to the approval-decision route every other kind already uses. Plain English throughout: a `MEMORY_CATEGORY_LABELS` table maps the schema's own category strings (`decisione`, `fatto`, `lezione`, …) to the words CUBE-009 asks for ("Decision", "Fact", "Lesson"), and `cube`/`promotion_state`/`contamination` never appear outside a `<details>` a person opens on purpose — the same progressive-disclosure shape §11's own worked example describes.
**A naming collision found and resolved, not invented.** `id="view-memory"` already existed — a manual, hand-written "memories" panel (title/content/tags, `state.memories`, `POST /api/v1/memories`) nested inside the Knowledge destination, reachable and functioning, just never a nav destination of its own. Two elements cannot share one id; renamed to `id="memory-notes-block"` (only its wrapper id — no id any JS/CSS selector referenced, verified by grep before touching it — and no behavioural change), heading text changed from "Memory" to "Notes" for the same reason, and the two features are now named distinctly in the product: **Notes** (hand-written, pinned, a person's own) vs. **Memory** (written automatically at the end of a session, never hand-edited — §11: "Non si scrive mai una memoria a mano"). This is the SAME two-store distinction `D-0263`'s own header already drew in code; this phase is what makes it visible in the product too.
**Three independent hardcoded copies of the destination/route lists found and reconciled**, each a real, working static check that would otherwise have gone stale silently: `tools/browser-e2e.mjs`'s `DESTINATIONS`/`LEGACY` and its "twelve destinations" assertion (now thirteen), `tools/accessibility-audit.mjs`'s `DESTINATIONS`, `tools/computed-style-snapshot.mjs`'s `DESTINATIONS`, and `services/reference-control-plane/test/webui-markup-structure.test.mjs`'s `DESTINATIONS`/`DEMOTED`/`RETIRED_ROUTES` (this one reads `app.js` directly rather than duplicating it by hand, but still carried its own separate lists of which routes are destinations vs. retired — `'memory'` had to leave `RETIRED_ROUTES` and `'view-memory'` had to leave `DEMOTED` for the same reason as the id rename above). None of these were guessed at: each was found by actually running the check and reading what broke.
**Two real, reproducible bugs found live-verifying this with the browser E2E suite, both fixed — neither in the Memory destination itself.** (1) `clickOrExplain()`'s `page.click(selector)` threw "Node is detached from document" reproducibly (3/3 runs) at the approval-queue Approve button, traced via the full stack trace to Puppeteer's own `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded → isIntersectingViewport → assertConnectedElement` chain: `page.click()` resolves a remote element handle, THEN scrolls it into view before dispatching, a real round trip with real elapsed time between "found" and "clicked" — and a re-render landing in that gap detaches the handle's node. Previously masked because `refreshApprovals()`'s only network call was synchronous-fast in-memory; `D-0263` made one of its four sources (`memoryService.listCandidates()`) a genuine PostgreSQL round trip, and that extra handful of milliseconds was enough to expose the race. Fixed by making `clickOrExplain()` dispatch an in-page `document.querySelector(sel).click()` instead — a single synchronous browser-side operation immune to this class of race regardless of what causes the re-render, and not a workaround for symptoms since it also drops an unneeded scroll-into-view (the existing geometry check already establishes visibility via `getBoundingClientRect`, which needs no scroll). (2) A second, independent bug in the SAME underlying cause: starting a workflow run's own click handler calls `loadWorkflows()` THEN `refreshApprovals()` in sequence, but the test's `waitForFunction` only watched the run list (which `loadWorkflows()` finishes first) — reading the approval strip immediately afterward raced `refreshApprovals()`'s own now-real network fetch and saw "Approvals: 0" instead of "Approvals: 1". Fixed with an explicit `waitForFunction` on the strip's own text (the same pattern already used elsewhere in this file), not a fixed delay. A third defensive fix — a latest-call-wins token guard added to `refreshApprovals()` itself, so an older overlapping call can never clobber a newer one's DOM update — is independently sound (a real duplicate-fetch race was observed live: two `/api/v1/approvals` GETs one millisecond apart) but did NOT resolve either reproduced failure on its own; kept because it closes a real class of bug regardless, disclosed honestly as not the fix that mattered here.
**Rejected.** Hiding the Keep/Discard buttons from roles without `agent.manage` (memory promotion decisions reuse the SAME shared, blanket-permission-gated `/api/v1/approvals/:id/decision` route every other approval kind already uses — widening or narrowing that one shared gate for one kind risks the other three and was not asked for; the existing `approvalCard()` already shows Approve/Reject unconditionally on the client with the server as the actual authority, and this destination follows the identical, already-established pattern). Building a separate manual "write a memory" affordance on this destination: explicitly forbidden by §11 ("mai a mano").
**Evidence.** Unit: `npm test` **1284/1285** (1 pre-existing unrelated skip; `webui-markup-structure.test.mjs`'s 36 tests, including the three updated for the new destination, all pass). `npm run lint` 255 files / 0 errors. **Live, in a real Chromium via Puppeteer, not just the DOM** (`tools/run-browser-e2e.sh`, disposable probe, PostgreSQL data plane): full browser E2E suite **334/334 PASS** (up from 235/238 on first attempt before the two real bugs above were found and fixed — the Memory route itself passed its own seven structural checks on the very first run, including document title, on-screen render, and zero console/failed-request errors), and the separate accessibility audit **27/27 PASS** (contrast across 9 themes, keyboard reachability, focus indicators, 24×24 targets, RTL, reduced motion — the Memory destination included in every sweep since it is walked as one of the now-thirteen `DESTINATIONS`).
**Deploy.** `docker stop -t 60` → `postgres.stopped clean:true` → backup `BACKUPS/runtime_pre_memory_webui_deploy_20260730T173434Z.tar.gz` (12.9 MB) → §5a (older rollback `memory-model-swap-...T170329Z` removed, predecessor renamed to `.rollback-memory-webui-20260730T173434Z`) → new container from the full `docker inspect` JSON. **Clean on the first attempt**: `Up (healthy)` at 12s, `data-plane.ready migrations:19 rls_tables:18`, `data-plane.workspace-projected ensured:true`, `/livez`/`/readyz` 200/200, hardening intact, `RestartCount:0`. Byte identity of both changed files confirmed via `docker cp` + `diff`. Post-deploy inventory: exactly 2 `noesar-evolution*` containers.
**Reversal cost.** None on live data: pure frontend + one renamed markup id, no schema change, no data written by this phase itself.
**Status.** `CUBE-009` closed and verified live, live in a real browser. **This closes `MASTER_PROJECT/14_MEMORIA_A_CUBI.md`'s entire acceptance matrix — `CUBE-001` through `CUBE-009` are now all built and verified live.** Block C is complete. `CUBE-005`'s one disclosed residual (the original `vector_entries` defect, independent of the cubes) remains open by design, named in `§9.1` as out of scope for the cubes themselves. `14 §9.6` point 9 (consolidation layers, day/month/year) was never in the acceptance matrix and is explicitly deferred — the doc's own words: "ultimo — prima serve materiale da consolidare," and there is none yet in production (`embedding_models`/`memory_records` are empty in the live product; this whole block proved the mechanism, not populated it). The multi-phase plan's own next step (`docs/SESSION_HANDOFF.md`'s header) is pausa 1.

## D-0266 · Block D1 — the Research destination built on the existing gate (`UI-080…096`), egress opened as a pluggable provider, not a vendor — 2026-07-31
**Decision.** Owner authorised opening real egress for Ricerca after the intent/content gate (`D-0222`) was found to have no dispatcher behind it. `research.mjs` (new): `runResearchReport()` — intent gate → designated external `tools` connector (reused, not duplicated — same consent/HTTPS/SSRF-guarded mechanism `agent-service.mjs`/`tool-executor.mjs` already built) → content gate on the answer → ephemeral, revocable, session-gated report (`ResearchReportStore`, in-memory by design — a restart revoking every live link is the declared behaviour). `RefusalRegistry` makes UI-096 real (a refusal is contestable only by the person it was shown to). No candidate's evidence/quality is synthesised by this product — a malformed provider answer is refused (`kind:INTERNAL`), never patched with defaults. `apps/webui-static`: the already-declared Research page gets its inputs (goal + removable criteria chips), a provider-designation panel (reuses `provider.manage`), and outcome rendering for all three gate outcomes plus a deep-linkable report (`#/research?report=<id>`).
**Why.** UI-080…089 needs real dispatch or the gate in front of it is decorative; the platform law (`CLAUDE10.md` §16) forbids a vendor baked into the code, so the provider is configured and consented like any other connector — UI-089's "declared egress" is then free (`privacy.mjs` already discloses a consented external tool).
**Rejected.** A parallel HTTP client + credential store for the provider (duplicates `tool-executor.mjs`'s SSRF guard, consent gate and vault for no reason). A built-in search vendor (violates the platform law; no key exists to hardcode honestly anyway).
**Evidence.** `research.test.mjs` (new, 12/12): both gates always called on PROCEED, intent REFUSE never dispatches (UI-095), content REFUSE discards an already-fetched report, ASK dispatches nothing, unconfigured/unconsented provider refused honestly, malformed candidate refused not patched, store expiry/revoke/contest-ownership. **Real bug found by the full suite, not review**: a bare `match = ...` (no `let`) in two new routes collided with a `let match` declared 800 lines later in the same function scope — TDZ, `ReferenceError` on every single request regardless of route, caught by 67 unrelated test failures across the whole suite. Fixed by scoping the two matches to their own names. `npm test` 1296/1297 (1 pre-existing skip, up from 1285), `npm run lint` 257 files / 0 errors. **Live, real Chromium**: browser E2E 334/334, accessibility audit 27/27 (14th destination walked in both).
**Deploy.** `docker stop -t 60` → `postgres.stopped clean:true` → backup `BACKUPS/runtime_pre_research_deploy_20260731T003927Z.tar.gz` (12.9 MB) → §5a (rollback `memory-webui-...T173434Z` removed, predecessor renamed to `.rollback-research-20260731T003927Z`) → new container from the full `docker inspect` JSON. `Up (healthy)` at 12s, `migrations:19 rls_tables:18`, `/livez`/`/readyz` 200/200, hardening intact, `RestartCount:0`, byte identity of all 5 changed/new files confirmed. Exactly 2 project containers.
**Reversal cost.** None on live data: no schema change, `state.tools`/`state.settings.researchProviderToolId` unset in production (no provider registered yet), `ResearchReportStore` is in-memory and empty at every restart regardless.
**Status.** Built, installed and verified live. `UI-080…096` closed. Open by design: no research provider is registered on this installation — an operator action, not a code gap (same posture as the reasoning provider). Item 5 of the pending backlog (stale `deferred_items` entry, timezone/locale pane) also corrected this session — see `PROJECT_STATE.json`.

## D-0267 · Block D2 — the CodeN Evolution TUI's sessions commands (`UI-050`) — 2026-07-31
**Decision.** `session-protocol.mjs` gains three dispatch methods — `sessions.list`/`sessions.get`/`sessions.action` — calling the SAME `contextGraph` instance the HTTP bridge's `/api/v1/sessions*` routes already use, so a session archived/binned/restored from either transport is the same fact, not two. `tools/tui-client.mjs` gains `sessions [place] [page]`/`session-show <n>`/`session-archive <n…|all>`/`session-delete <n…|all>`/`session-restore <n…|all>`/`session-undone`, resolving `<n>` against the last list shown, exactly like the browser's numbered rows; `session-delete` sends `bin` or `purge` depending on whether the last list shown was the bin, matching the browser's own Delete-key rule exactly. Every destructive-or-moving action names what and how many before asking `Confirm? [y/N]` with no default (UI-008/051/052) — a bare Enter cancels.
**Why.** `UI-050` (Critica): every session action needs a keyboard form AND a TUI command; only the keyboard half existed (`D-0266`'s handoff named this the next action). `CE-020` ("every capability exercised by the TUI") fails on session management until this closes.
**Rejected.** A stateful `select`/`apply` command pair mirroring the browser's checkboxes (`Space`/`Ctrl+A`) — a terminal line already expresses a set in one shot (`session-delete 2 5 7`, or `all`), so a second command just to stage a selection would be state the CLI does not need. `restore` was also rejected as the verb name — it already means "undo a promoted workspace-action run"; `session-restore` avoids the collision.
**Evidence.** `session-protocol.test.mjs` +6 tests over the real socket transport (list reflects a live-created conversation, get by id, a mixed batch reports one applied/one refused rather than all-or-nothing, the five-verb enum is enforced, empty-ids refused). New `tui-client-sessions.test.mjs`, 9 tests against a stubbed `session`/`reader` (no socket, no product): number-to-id resolution, `all`, out-of-range refusal, the confirm gate genuinely blocking on a bare Enter, and the bin-vs-purge branch. Full suite **1312/1313** (1 pre-existing skip, up from 1297), ESLint **258 files 0 errors**, `scripts/test.sh` **10/10**, seeded-defect **19/19**, `auth-http-smoke`/`http-smoke` PASS, `MANIFEST.sha256` **5880/5880** (4 changed hashes updated, 1 new file appended).
**Deploy.** `docker stop -t 60` → `postgres.stopped clean:true` confirmed in the log → backup (12.9 MB, service stopped) → §5a (older rollback `memory-webui-...T003927Z` removed, predecessor renamed to `.rollback-sessions-tui-20260731T022844Z`) → new container from the full `docker inspect` HostConfig JSON. `Up (healthy)`, `migrations:19 rls_tables:18`, `/livez`/`/readyz` 200/200, hardening intact (`ReadonlyRootfs:true CapDrop:[ALL] RestartCount:0`), image bytes match the tree for both changed source files. Live probe against the deployed container (unauthenticated, no real session touched): `sessions.list` answers `UNAUTHENTICATED` — the new method is genuinely wired and gated, not merely present in the image. Exactly 2 project containers after cleanup.
**Reversal cost.** None on live data: additive dispatch methods and CLI commands only, no schema change, no change to any existing method's behaviour.
**Status.** Built, installed and verified live. `UI-050` closed for the sessions surface. `CE-020` still open for the agent-panels half (`UI-054`, `F1…F9`/`/pannello <nome>`) — that is Block D3, alongside Voice (`D-0123`).
