The module's own service token (`module-credentials/debug-evolution.token`) authenticates a real HTTP request to the catalog route — `200`. `POST /api/v1/debug-evolution/rescan` without a session answers `401` (auth required), not `409` (module inactive) — confirms the module-active gate added in this decision is live and correct. `debug-evolution`, `atomd`, `atom-evolution-model` containers: unaffected, all healthy throughout. Exactly two `noesar-evolution*` containers survive (§5a).
**Reversal cost.** None on live data: no schema change, no migration. Reverting restores environment-driven wiring; an installed module's `state.json` is forward-compatible (the old code reads `status:"uninstalled"` as neither installed nor active through `loadModuleState`, which is the same conclusion). Rollback: `docker stop -t 60 noesar-evolution && docker rename noesar-evolution <aside> && docker start noesar-evolution.rollback-module-console-proxy-20260801T133906Z` — recreate with the same hardened `HostConfig` this decision restored, not the incomplete one from the first attempt.
**Status.** Built, installed and verified live.

## D-0284 · Phase 2 of Debug Evolution's own plan, first slice — discovery+skeptic, and a correction to which ATOM surfaces actually fit — 2026-08-01
**Decision.** Debug Evolution's own plan (Owner s302) named Phase 2 as "agenti — un compito ciascuno, lettura riga per riga; il verdetto vero/falso-positivo NON va inventato: è ATOM (superfici `classify`/`confidence`/`evidence`/`expect`)." Two things were found wrong with that sentence on inspection, both corrected here rather than carried forward silently. First: Debug Evolution already HAS the entire apparatus this phase needs — a formal finding lifecycle (`findings.state`, `TRANSITIONS`, `can_transition()`), an evidence ledger with 11 typed kinds including `AI_HYPOTHESIS`/`COUNTER_EVIDENCE`, working `POST .../evidence` and `.../transition` endpoints (the "Evidence Court", `D-0280`), and six agent roles already NAMED in `de_v2/app.py`'s `AGENTS` constant (`discovery`, `security`, `skeptic`, `reproducer`, `root-cause`, `patch-review`) but never wired to anything. Zero changes to the `.pyz` were needed. Second: the four surfaces named for the verdict are wrong for this job. `classify(plan)`, `confidence(plan, results)` and `expect(plan)` are all signed on `Plan` — a code-CHANGE plan, steps/files/commands/blast-radius (`ATOM_EVOLUTION/contract/noesar-reasoning/src/lib.rs`) — not on a static-analysis finding; using them would mean minting a fake "plan to inspect this finding" for no reason but to match a surface name someone wrote down before reading the contract. The two surfaces that fit without forcing anything are `hypothesize(intent, gathered) -> Hypothesis[]` and `evidence(claim) -> Evidence`. `Hypothesis` already carries BOTH `supporting` evidence and a genuine `contrary` search (`NOT_SOUGHT`/`NONE_FOUND`/`FOUND{evidence}`) in one answer — `discovery` and `skeptic`, the two roles this slice implements, turn out to be one call, not two.
**What was built.** `debug-evolution-triage.mjs` (new): pure conversion only — an `IntentFrame` from a finding (excluding remediation and execution from `nonGoals`, matching the module's own catalog manifest), the finding's own scanner output offered back as `gathered` evidence, and `Hypothesis` → Debug Evolution evidence rows (`supporting` → `AI_HYPOTHESIS`, `contrary:FOUND` → `COUNTER_EVIDENCE`, `NOT_SOUGHT`/`NONE_FOUND` → no row, because neither is evidence of anything). `debug-evolution-bridge.mjs` gained `triageUnclassifiedFindings(router)`, the orchestration sibling to `rescanNoesarEvolutionProjects()`: every `DETECTED` finding across the already-registered NOESAR EVOLUTION projects, one `hypothesize()` call each, every resulting evidence row submitted, then one attempt at `DETECTED -> HYPOTHESIZED` with `actor:'atom'` (Debug Evolution's own state machine decides whether it is legal — this module never overrides it). New `POST /api/v1/debug-evolution/triage` (owner+CSRF, same `isModuleActive` gate `D-0283` added to rescan). New "Triage findings" button on the module card, shown only when the module is active — Owner asked for the button now rather than API-only like Rescan (still has none). `router.identity()` was caught mid-build always answering for the reference provider regardless of routing (`#reference.identity()`, not routed) — the response reports `provenance()` instead, which is what actually says whether ATOM or the reference provider answered.
**Why this and not the alternatives.** Manual trigger, same posture as Rescan and for the same reason: cost/latency per finding on this deployment is not yet measured, so this is a deliberate click, not something that fires after every scan ("misura prima, ottimizza dopo"). All six declared agent roles at once — rejected for this slice: `reproducer`/`patch-review` reach toward execution and patch application, both explicitly excluded by the module's own manifest (`owner-module-catalog.mjs`'s `excluded_use`) and by nothing this session verified is safe to automate yet. Debug Evolution calling ATOM directly instead of NOESAR bridging — rejected for the same reason `D-0280` gave for the module's own credential: one authentication, and it is NOESAR's; Debug Evolution never holds an ATOM token.
**Evidence.** New `debug-evolution-triage.test.mjs` (10 unit tests): the intent excludes remediation/execution and asks for a genuine counter-evidence search; gathered evidence is never empty; `SUPPORTED`/`UNSUPPORTED_INFERENCE` convert to rows with the real locator/rationale text, never a fabricated source; neither ATOM evidence kind is ever a Debug Evolution `PRIMARY` type (mechanically, not by promise); `NOT_SOUGHT`/`NONE_FOUND` add no counter-evidence row, `FOUND` does. New `debug-evolution-triage-http.test.mjs` (4 tests, full `server.mjs` boot, a stub ATOM answering the REAL wire shape from `conformance/wire-vectors.json` + `wire.rs`, a stub stateful Debug Evolution): 401/403 without session/CSRF; the one `DETECTED` finding is visited, the already-`CONFIRMED` one is not, two real evidence rows land with the real counter-evidence text unchanged, the transition lands with `actor:'atom'` and Debug Evolution's own new state (`HYPOTHESIZED`) comes back, `provenance` confirms ATOM (not the reference provider) answered; a second run re-reads the stub's own now-changed state and correctly triages nothing. Full suite **1448/1449** (1 pre-existing skip, 0 failed, +14 new). ESLint **286 files 0 errors 0 warnings**.
**Reversal cost.** None on live data: no schema change on either side, no `.pyz` touched. Reverting removes the route, the bridge functions and the button; Debug Evolution's own findings/evidence/transitions are untouched by a revert since nothing here can write anything Debug Evolution's own `can_transition()` did not already agree to.
**Status.** Built and verified in test; **not deployed live** — code, tests and docs only, pending the Owner's word on the rebuild (same posture as `D-0283` before its own deploy this session). Phase 2's remaining four roles (`reproducer`, `root-cause`, `patch-review`, and `security`) are open, named rather than silently deferred.

## D-0285 · Second slice of Debug Evolution's own Phase 2 — security+root-cause, and a third correction to what the evidence is allowed to say — 2026-08-01
**Decision.** `security` and `root-cause`, two more of the six agent roles Debug Evolution already declares (`de_v2/app.py`'s `AGENTS`) but has never wired, join `discovery`+`skeptic` (`D-0284`) as pure-reasoning triage roles — still zero `.pyz` changes, still no execution. `debug-evolution-triage.mjs` gains `findingAsSecurityIntent()` (asks whether the location is reachable from a trust boundary an attacker could reach) and `findingAsRootCauseIntent()` (asks for the specific causal defect, not a restatement of the symptom), exported together with the existing (renamed) `findingAsDiscoveryIntent()` as `TRIAGE_ROLE_INTENTS`. `triageFinding()` in `debug-evolution-bridge.mjs` now calls `hypothesize()` once per role (three calls, not six — `discovery`'s call already covers `skeptic` via `Hypothesis.contrary`), submits every resulting evidence row tagged with which role produced it (`metadata.role`), then attempts one `DETECTED -> HYPOTHESIZED` transition with a rationale citing all three roles' statements. Same manual trigger, same route, same "Triage findings" button — richer evidence per click, not a new surface.

**The correction, found before writing code.** This session's own proposal for `security`, made while scoping with the Owner, described it as producing `SEMANTIC_REACHABILITY` evidence. On inspection of `de_v2/core.py`'s own taxonomy, that was wrong: `SEMANTIC_REACHABILITY` sits in the same family as `STATIC_ANALYZER`/`DETERMINISTIC_REPRODUCER`/`RUNTIME_DETECTOR`/`FORMAL_PROOF` — evidence a TOOL or an EXECUTION produced, not a model's opinion — and it is the type `can_transition()` specifically requires for `HYPOTHESIZED -> REACHABILITY_CHECKED`. Tagging an ATOM answer with it would claim a rigor never performed, the same mistake `classify`/`confidence`/`expect` would have been in `D-0284`. Both new roles therefore add `AI_HYPOTHESIS` rows, exactly like `discovery`, and neither role's call attempts any transition past `HYPOTHESIZED` — `REACHABILITY_CHECKED` stays a tool's job or a human's, never manufactured by relabelling an LLM guess.

**The other two roles, scoped and declined for now.** `reproducer` (needs `DETERMINISTIC_REPRODUCER`/`RUNTIME_DETECTOR` evidence for `REPRODUCED` — i.e., something actually run) and `patch-review` (needs `PATCH_TEST`+`INDEPENDENT_TEST` for `PATCH_VERIFIED` — i.e., a patch that does not yet exist anywhere, tested for real) both require genuine code execution. NOESAR EVOLUTION already has a real sandbox for exactly this (`EXECUTE`, `D-0249`/`D-0250`/`D-0253` — a dedicated binary, capability-token gated, Rust-mirrored), left disabled per installation by explicit design (`execute-sandbox-config.mjs`'s own header: "reversing it was never the Owner's alone to decide on this one installation's behalf, because NOESAR EVOLUTION is installed by other people on their own hosts"). Owner declined to enable it as a side effect of this feature — a real security decision stays a decision, not a default flipped in passing. Both roles remain named as open, not silently dropped.

**Evidence.** `debug-evolution-triage.test.mjs`: 4 new tests (security/root-cause intent shape, `TRIAGE_ROLE_INTENTS` structure, security-role evidence still tagged `AI_HYPOTHESIS` never `SEMANTIC_REACHABILITY`) plus the existing `hypothesisToEvidenceRows` tests extended to assert the new `role` tag. `debug-evolution-triage-http.test.mjs`: the stub ATOM now answers three DIFFERENT `intent.goal`s distinctly (matching what the real sidecar would face); the end-to-end test confirms exactly three `hypothesize()` calls (not six), four evidence rows with the right role tags and real text reaching Debug Evolution unchanged, one transition with all three roles cited in its rationale, and `provenance()` showing ATOM (not the reference provider) answered all three. Full suite **1452/1453** (1 pre-existing skip, 0 failed, +4 net over `D-0284`'s 1448). ESLint **286 files 0 errors 0 warnings** (no new files this decision, only extended ones).
**Reversal cost.** None on live data: no schema change on either side, no `.pyz` touched, and every write is still evidence Debug Evolution's own `can_transition()` already agreed to. Reverting removes the two intent builders and their calls; `discovery`+`skeptic` keep working exactly as `D-0284` shipped them.
**Status.** Built and verified in test; deployment left to the Owner's word, same posture as every deploy this session that preceded an explicit go-ahead.

## D-0286 · Debug Evolution's Phase 3, finished — remote targets over SSH, credential never leaves NOESAR's vault — 2026-08-01
**Decision.** "Bersagli remoti via SSH, credenziali dal vault NOESAR, mai su disco nel modulo" (Owner s302's own plan for Debug Evolution). Debug Evolution never sees a credential: NOESAR runs `ssh-keyscan` at registration (`remote-target-fetch.mjs::keyscanHost()`) to capture the host's OWN public key — not just its fingerprint, which alone would be security theatre, since `ssh`/`scp` verify a connection against the real key via `known_hosts`, not against a hash of it. The Owner confirms the fingerprint out of band, then supplies a private key (`remote-target-registry.mjs`, the same `CredentialVault` every other credential in this product already uses — one authentication, one encryption-at-rest key). Fetching (`fetchRemoteTarget()`) runs real `scp -r`, verified against the pinned key with `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes` never relaxed, both the key and the pinned host key written only to this process's own tmpfs `/tmp` for the duration of the call and unconditionally removed after — unlike `sandbox-runner.mjs`'s own temp files ("never contains a secret"), this one does, so cleanup here is `finally`, not best-effort. `openssh-client` (real `ssh-keyscan`/`scp`, spawned via argv, never a shell string) is the one new system dependency — no third-party SSH library, matching this codebase's own stated convention. The fetched tarball uploads to a NEW Debug Evolution endpoint, `POST /api/v2/projects/import` (the one `.pyz` change this decision needed — Phase 2, D-0284/D-0285, needed none), which extracts with Python's `tarfile` `filter='data'` (PEP 706, stdlib since 3.12 — CPython's own vetted defence against a member escaping the destination, not a rule this module invented) and then calls the EXISTING `register()` unchanged. `AI_STATE_VERSION` 3→4 (`remoteTargets`, purely additive, same idiom as every prior bump).

**A defect found and fixed along the way, not scope creep.** Stopping `debug-evolution` for this deploy exited `137` (SIGKILL after the stop timeout), not `0`. Root cause: `appliance/run.py` starts the real server via `subprocess.call()`, which does not forward signals to the child it spawns — `docker stop`'s SIGTERM killed `run.py` (PID 1) immediately, orphaning the actual server process until Docker's own grace period expired and SIGKILLed the whole cgroup. The server's own graceful shutdown (`de_v2/cli.py`: `finally: srv.shutdown(); app.engine.shutdown(); app.store.db.close()` — exactly the path a prior session's segfault fix, s302, made safe) never ran, because nothing ever reached it. SQLite's own journal made this non-corrupting in practice (`PRAGMA integrity_check` read `ok`, 17 projects/84 findings intact, both before AND after this fix), which is a property of SQLite, not a reason to leave an orphaned-then-SIGKILLed shutdown as the normal deploy path. Fixed: `run.py` now runs the server via `Popen`, installs a SIGTERM/SIGINT handler that forwards `SIGINT` (not SIGTERM verbatim — the child has no SIGTERM handler of its own either, and SIGINT is the signal `except KeyboardInterrupt` already catches correctly), and waits for the real exit code. Verified live on a throwaway container before touching the production one: `docker stop -t 10` completed in 0.145s with `ExitCode=0`, against the prior behaviour of running the full 30s timeout into a `137`.

**Why this and not the alternatives.** Debug Evolution fetching directly over SSH (a credential handed to it, even short-lived) — rejected, same reasoning as D-0280's "one authentication, and it is NOESAR's": the module's own manifest already narrows its surface deliberately, and giving it SSH client code + credential material even transiently reopens exactly what that manifest closes. A pure-JS SSH2 library instead of `openssh-client` — rejected: a well-audited, minimal system package the project already trusts elsewhere (Debian, same base as everything else) has a smaller trust surface than an arbitrary third-party SSH protocol implementation added to the security-sensitive control plane. Disabling `StrictHostKeyChecking` for convenience — rejected outright; a changed host identity refusing the connection (`HOST_KEY_MISMATCH`, proven live against a real sshd) is the entire point of pinning a key at registration. Deleting the fetched copy after each scan — Owner confirmed it should persist like a local project does, a re-fetch overwrites the same directory (the target's own stable id as the slug) rather than merge with files a since-deleted remote file would otherwise leave behind forever. `reproducer`/`patch-review` (the two Phase 2 roles requiring real code execution) enabling NOESAR's existing `EXECUTE` sandbox as a side effect of this feature — the Owner declined explicitly; that remains its own decision, not a side effect of Phase 3 shipping.

**Evidence.** Nothing about the SSH half is mocked. `remote-target-fetch.test.mjs` (5 tests) and `remote-target-http.test.mjs` (7 tests) both stand up a REAL local `sshd` (this host carries a full OpenSSH client+server) with a real generated host key and client keypair: real `ssh-keyscan` captures the real key and a fingerprint that matches `ssh-keygen -lf` computed independently; a real `scp -r` fetches a real nested directory tree and the exact file contents survive; a host key that no longer matches the pinned one is refused as `HOST_KEY_MISMATCH`, not silently trusted; a key the server does not authorise is refused as `AUTH_FAILED`, not a hang; the full HTTP route chain (register → real keyscan → activate with the real key → fetch-and-scan with real `scp` → upload lands at a stub Debug Evolution with the real bytes unchanged) all pass end to end. `remote-target-registry.test.mjs` (11 tests): the vault round-trip is byte-identical, `encryptedCredential` never appears in any public read, activation/rotation/removal refuse the right way on the wrong state. The Debug Evolution import endpoint was proven live against the actual `.pyz` before packaging it: a valid tarball registers a real project; a crafted tarball with a `../../etc/evil_payload` member is refused with `HTTP 400` and Python's own explanation of exactly what it caught, nothing escapes anywhere on the host; re-fetching the same slug replaces the old files outright, confirmed by their absence afterward; an invalid slug is refused before any extraction. `ai-state-migration.test.mjs` extended (3 new tests, 12/12 total): the 3→4 migration is additive, the full 1→4 chain still works, a state already at 4 is unchanged. Full suite **1477/1478** (1 pre-existing skip, 0 failed, +25 net over D-0285's 1452). ESLint **291 files 0 errors 0 warnings**.
**Deploy.** Both products, in order. `debug-evolution:1.1.0-remote-targets` (`FROM` the same `run.py`/SHA256SUMS-verified 31/31 lineage as `:1.1.0-scan-engine`, plus the import endpoint and the SIGTERM fix): volume backed up (`state/BACKUPS/debug_evolution_data_pre_remote_targets_<ts>.tar.gz`, 699 MB) → §5a → recreated with the exact original `HostConfig` — healthy, `PRAGMA integrity_check` `ok`, 17 projects/84 findings intact, the new import endpoint live (`400` on a zero-byte body, exactly its own declared validation). `noesar-evolution:phase4-debug-evolution-remote-targets` (`FROM :phase4-debug-evolution-security-root-cause`, +`openssh-client`, 24 layers): stop → `postgres.stopped clean:true`, exit 0 → backup (`BACKUPS/runtime_pre_debug_evolution_remote_targets_deploy_<ts>.tar.gz`, 13 MB, `schemaVersion:3` confirmed on disk pre-deploy — the REAL production file this migration had to load) → §5a → recreated — healthy on the first attempt (fourth deploy this session, no surprises), `data-plane.ready migrations:19 rls_tables:18 production_ready:true` unchanged, `ssh-keyscan`/`scp`/`ssh-keygen` present live, both remote-target routes reachable and correctly gated (`401` without a session). **Not verified live**: the full authenticated Owner-session walkthrough (register→activate→fetch-and-scan against a real remote, through the real UI) — no password/TOTP available on this installation, the same limitation named honestly for every feature this session (`D-0279`/`D-0282`/`D-0283`/`D-0284`/`D-0285`). What IS proven live and not only in test: the schema migration against the real installed file, both products' health and data integrity across the deploy, the SIGTERM fix, and every subprocess call in isolation.
**Reversal cost.** None on live data for either product: `AI_STATE_VERSION` 4 is additive and the migration is one-directional by design (a rollback to a pre-4 image reads a `remoteTargets`-carrying file the same way any older build reads a file with fields it does not know — extra keys are not validated away, only the `REQUIRED_COLLECTIONS` this build's own code demands). Debug Evolution's `run.py` fix and import endpoint touch no existing table or route. Both rollback paths follow this session's own established pattern — the predecessor container renamed, not removed, image preserved.
**Status.** Built, installed and verified live. Debug Evolution's own 5-phase plan (Owner s302) is now complete through Phase 3; Phase 4 (cube+vector memory in the module's own DB) remains open and explicitly named, not started.

## D-0287 · Debug Evolution's real detectors wired — 20 external static analyzers, not the Owner's own 5-phase plan — 2026-08-01
**Decision.** The Owner asked a direct question — how many tools does Debug Evolution really run, what level is it at — and the honest answer was hard: `discover_toolpacks()` (`de_v2/app.py`) only ever ran `doctor` on the eight toolpacks under `appliance/toolpacks/*.pyz` to populate the dashboard; the scan engine (`de_v2/scan.py`) never called a single one. Every finding in the live database (84 of them, all `DE-HARDCODED-SECRET`) came from `program-genome`, five hand-written regexes in `core.py::scan_text()`. The toolpacks themselves were not stubs — each ships a real `ToolRunner` (subprocess isolation, timeout, output limits, an offline-by-default `secure_environment()` that sets `GOPROXY=off`/`PIP_NO_INDEX=1`/... unless explicitly told otherwise), real SARIF/JSON parsers per tool, and a `run <tool_id> <root> --json-output <path>` CLI — just never called. This decision wires that CLI into the scan engine for real, for the 20 of the 29 catalogued tools that are both offline (no `network_required`) and do not execute project code (`executes_project_code: false`): 11 from `static-quality.pyz` (`ruff`, `mypy`, `pyright`, `typescript`, `shellcheck`, `hadolint`, `semgrep-ce`, `clang-tidy`, `cppcheck`, `checkstyle`, `luacheck`) and 9 from `security-supply-chain.pyz` (`bandit`, `gosec`, `semgrep-security`, `detect-secrets`, `gitleaks`, `trufflehog`, `checkov`, `tfsec`, `kube-linter`). Findings land in the real Evidence Court as `STATIC_ANALYZER` evidence (`core.py::make_tool_finding()`) and attempt one transition, `DETECTED → HYPOTHESIZED` — never further; `can_transition()`'s own gate already refuses `CONFIRMED` on static evidence alone ("AI or static evidence alone cannot confirm"), so this needed no new restraint, only the right evidence type.

**Explicitly out of scope, an Owner decision confirmed twice via `AskUserQuestion`, not an oversight.** Eight tools that phone a vulnerability database on every scan (`pip-audit`, `cargo-audit`, `cargo-deny`, `govulncheck`, `npm-audit`, `osv-scanner`, `trivy-fs`, `grype-dir`) stay unwired — `security-supply-chain.pyz`'s own `ToolRunner` already self-blocks them with `BLOCKED_REQUIRES_NETWORK_AUTHORIZATION` unless a caller passes `--allow-network`, which this wiring never does; a second line of defence behind the decision, not a substitute for it. `syft-dir` (SBOM generation, `parser: "none"`) is not a finding source and was left out on that basis, not folded in silently. The other 56 tools (8 more `static-quality`/`security-supply-chain` tools that DO execute project code — `eslint`, `pylint`, `cargo-clippy`, `staticcheck`, `go-vet`, `rubocop`, `phpstan`, `stylelint` — plus all of `dynamic-analysis.pyz` and `fuzzing-symbolic.pyz`) require NOESAR's `EXECUTE` sandbox, which the Owner declined to enable as a side effect of D-0285 and declined again here — untouched.

**A real defect found live, in a toolpack that had never been exercised, not invented.** `static-quality.pyz`'s `parse_shellcheck()` expected a bare JSON list; `shellcheck --format=json1` (the format its own command actually uses) wraps results in `{"comments": [...]}`. A real ShellCheck run against a real script with a real `SC2086` (unquoted variable) produced the finding on stdout and the parser silently dropped it — `isinstance(data, list)` was never true. This is not a wiring bug; the toolpack shipped with it, undetected because nothing had ever called `run shellcheck` against real output before. Fixed in `de_toolpack/parsers.py`: unwrap `.comments` when the top level is a dict. Verified live, both before and after: the same scan produced 86 findings before the fix, 87 after — the missing `SHELLCHECK:SC2086` finding, present.

**Why this and not the alternatives.** A hand-rolled secret/quality scanner extended file-by-file — rejected: eight already-built, independently-maintained analyzers (`gitleaks`, `bandit`, `mypy`, ...) parsing their own tools' real output are categorically more capable than any bespoke regex set, and the toolpacks already existed, tested, unused. Running all 29 catalogued tools regardless of network posture — rejected, see above; the Owner chose the 21-offline / 8-network split explicitly, not by default. A `'fast'`/`'normal'`/`'deep'` profile split for which of the 20 tools run — not arbitrary: `'fast'` runs only the seven tools each toolpack's own registry marks `enabled_by_default`; `'normal'` adds tools relevant to the languages/manifests actually present (derived from the same enumerated file list the per-file pass already built — no second filesystem walk); `'deep'` runs all 20, plus `trufflehog` (held back from `'normal'` because its filesystem detectors proved, live, deliberately more conservative than `gitleaks`'s — verified against a synthetic AKIA-shaped key that `gitleaks` caught and `trufflehog` did not, by design, not by defect). One project-level pass per tool per scan, not per file — re-starting a Python/Node/JVM process per file for tools that need whole-package context (`mypy`, `bandit`) would be fake throughput, the same reasoning `scan.py`'s own "why one worker" note already gives for the per-file pass.

**Evidence.** All 20 tools installed via checksum-verified binaries (apt for 4: `shellcheck`/`clang-tidy`/`cppcheck`/`checkstyle`; pip for 7: `ruff`/`mypy`/`pyright`/`semgrep`/`bandit`/`detect-secrets`/`checkov`; npm for 1: `typescript`; luarocks for 1: `luacheck`; 6 static Go binaries fetched from their own GitHub releases with SHA-256 cross-checked against the project's own published checksums where published, pinned from this build's own observed hash where not) — every one exercised individually against a real multi-language test repository (Python/Shell/Dockerfile/C/Terraform/Kubernetes/Go/Lua/Java) with a real, known issue per language before any wiring code was written. End-to-end: a `'deep'` scan through the real `de_v2` HTTP API attempted all 20 tools, completed all 20 cleanly (0 skipped, 0 errored, 0 timed out), produced 86→87 real findings (the shellcheck fix) with `STATIC_ANALYZER` evidence and `HYPOTHESIZED` transitions correctly recorded, run first against a scratch harness and then again against the actual production image via its real `run.py` entrypoint (not bypassed) with the actual `--no-auth` flag, confirming `docker stop -t 10` still exits in `0.145s`/`ExitCode 0` (D-0286's fix, unregressed). A further live scan against real production code — NOESAR EVOLUTION's own `reference-control-plane` source tree, 203 files — surfaced 138 real findings, most of them `detect-secrets: Secret Keyword` hits inside `*.test.mjs` files: almost certainly false positives on test fixtures shaped like credentials, landing at `HYPOTHESIZED` rather than asserted true, which is the Evidence Court working as designed, not a defect being claimed away.

**Deploy.** `debug-evolution` only — no NOESAR EVOLUTION file changed, no commit needed on that side. Image grew from 119 MB to 2.58 GB (`golang-go` for `gosec`, `default-jre-headless` for `checkstyle`, `checkov`'s own dependency tree, Node/npm for `typescript` — a real cost of 20 real analyzers, measured, not estimated). Backup (`BACKUPS/debug_evolution_data_pre_toolpack_wiring_<ts>.tar.gz`, 732 MB) → §5a → recreated with the exact original `HostConfig` (all five binds including the two read-only source-tree mounts, `--ip 172.22.0.2` pinned, `--restart unless-stopped`) → healthy on the first attempt, `PRAGMA integrity_check` `ok`, 17 projects/84 pre-existing findings intact. `debug-evolution.pyz` and `static-quality.pyz` both backed up under `.bak_pre_*` before editing (DEBUG_EVOLUTION's own convention — no git); `SHA256SUMS` updated for `Dockerfile`, `appliance/app/debug-evolution.pyz`, `appliance/toolpacks/static-quality.pyz`, verified 31/31 after.
**Reversal cost.** Low. The rollback container (`debug-evolution.rollback-remote-targets-<ts>`, image `debug-evolution:1.1.0-remote-targets`) is a straight `docker rename` + `docker start` away; the named volume was never reformatted, only read. `AI_STATE_VERSION`/schema untouched — this decision added no new SQLite table or column to `findings`/`evidence`, only new rows of an evidence type (`STATIC_ANALYZER`) the schema already declared.
**Status.** Built, installed and verified live. Not part of the Owner's own 5-phase plan (Phase 4, cube+vector memory, remains the one open phase of that plan) — this closes a gap the plan itself did not name: real tools existed, unwired, since before this session began.

## D-0288 · Debug Evolution's cube memory (Phase 4) — a real vocabulary shared with NOESAR, an intentionally empty vector index — 2026-08-01

**Decision.** Close the Owner's own 5-phase plan for Debug Evolution: a new `de_v2/memory.py` gives the module the same 4-cube / 9-category vocabulary NOESAR uses, with hooks in `core.py`/`scan.py`/`uplink.py`/`app.py`/webui. Assimilation is wired into `Store.add_evidence()`/`Store.transition()`, not into the agents — the triage agents run on the NOESAR side and arrive through the same HTTP writes the console uses, so intercepting at the `Store` catches them without the module knowing they exist. A verdict maps to cube `experience` (only terminal states + `CONFIRMED`, derived from `TRANSITIONS`, never hand-written); an agent hypothesis maps to cube `workshop`, written as *"agent X hypothesized Y"*, never as *"Y"* — the accepted fact is that the hypothesis was made, not that it is true, always `unverified`; a finished scan maps to cube `corpus` as `verified` measured numbers. `Uplink.recall()` is the module's only route into NOESAR's memory and there is no write-back counterpart — copying a NOESAR record in is an explicit, one-at-a-time act (`assimilate_from_noesar` → cube `library`, `derived=True`, contamination floor: a derivative is never cleaner than the source it cites).

**The vector index was built empty, on purpose.** Four options existed; the Owner chose "full architecture, empty index." The fact that decided it: NOESAR itself has no embedder (`memory-service.mjs:253`, *"No embedding pipeline exists in this product yet"*), and the model server answers `501 "This server does not support embeddings"` — measured, not assumed. Rejected without asking: using Qwen2.5-Coder (an instruct decoder, not trained for retrieval) as an encoder, or a lexical local embedder dressed up as semantic — both violate "no magic." The upgrade path is already wired (`register_model()`/`set_vector()`/`similar()` all work, verified with a 4-dimension toy model): turning on a real embedder later is configuration, not a rewrite — records do not move.

**Where NOESAR's own pattern was deliberately not copied.** NOESAR splits vectors into a `memory_vectors_1024` table because pgvector's `vector(384)` fixes width in the column's type. SQLite has no vector type; a `BLOB` declares no width, so width is checked at write time against `embedding_models.dimensions` and one table is enough — replicating NOESAR's split here would have been cargo-culting a constraint this engine does not have.

**Evidence.** 56 green checks (28 in-process + 28 HTTP against the built `.pyz`). Live on the real container: 17 projects intact; a `fast` scan over 145 real files produced a `corpus` record with the measured numbers; a `DE-HARDCODED-SECRET` inside a test fixture, judged `FALSE_POSITIVE` by the Court, landed correctly as a `lezione` (designed behavior, observed happening, not a project defect). `docker stop` in 153ms/exit 0 — D-0286's SIGTERM fix unregressed. Memory survives a restart. Zero assimilation failures.

**Deploy.** `debug-evolution:1.1.1-cube-memory`. Rollback preserved: container `debug-evolution-pre-cube-memory` (stopped, exit 0) + `debug-evolution.pyz.bak_pre_cube_memory_20260801T181135Z`. `SHA256SUMS` 31/31.
**Status.** Installed and verified live. This closed the Owner's original 5-phase plan for Debug Evolution.

## D-0289 · Code execution, switched on and fenced — Debug Evolution's first `CONFIRMED` finding ever — 2026-08-01

**Decision.** After D-0288, the module's Evidence Court had never once reached `CONFIRMED` in 250 findings — not by chance: all five primary-proof paths `can_transition()` accepts require observing a program actually run, and the module executed nothing. Wired a second container, `debug-evolution-runner`: same image, `--network none`, mounts only the `debug_evolution_sandbox` named volume — no private source trees, no `/run/noesar-credentials`. Verified live, not assumed: from the runner, NOESAR's LAN address, the internal network and the Internet are all unreachable, and the three sensitive paths do not exist inside it. Communication is a filesystem queue, never HTTP — any socket letting the console reach the runner would let the runner's untrusted children reach the console back, which runs with `REQUIRE_AUTH=false`.

**What the fence is not**, stated plainly in the module's own header: there is no mutual distrust between the worker and the code it runs — they share a uid. `job.json` is deleted before the tool starts (raises the cost of tampering) but the blast radius stands: a falsified result becomes a *finding*, and a finding is a thesis the Court still requires corroboration for. It cannot forge a token, reach the network, or touch the repo.

**A hole found and closed before the session ended.** The fence stopped the runner from *mounting* private sources, but a `dinamica` scan pointed by hand at `noesar_evolution` would have *copied* that tree into the sandbox instead. Closed with `refuse_dynamic_reason()`: execution is refused on any tree under a read-only mount, read live from `/proc/mounts` — not a hand-maintained path list, which would be wrong at the very next differently-shaped deployment. A read-only tree is a live source someone mounted to be read, not a copy imported to be run. Static scanning stays allowed (verified: 59,147 files over NOESAR_EVOLUTION, `DONE`). The correct on-ramp is `POST /api/v2/projects/import` (D-0286) → writable copy → `dinamica`.

**Three real defects found deploying, not invented.** (1) Root-owned volume: the runner crash-looped (`PermissionError: /var/lib/debug-evolution-sandbox/jobs`) — Docker copies ownership from the image path when it first populates an empty volume, and a path absent from the image leaves the volume root-owned; fixed in the Dockerfile, not just on the volume. (2) `node-trace-uncaught` and `python-faulthandler` require `--target`, which was only being passed to the probe, producing a `TOOL_ERROR` that looked like a broken tool — the entry point is now chosen by language and skipped before dispatch, with the reason stated, when none applies. (3) `fuzzing-symbolic.pyz` has no `run` verb (it has `fuzz-python`/`property`/`differential`/`boundary-seeds`/`run-external`) — a wrong assumption, so the pack was pulled from `SANDBOX_PACKS` with the reason recorded; wiring it is its own piece of work.

**Numbers counted, not estimated.** 67 tools across the toolpacks. Tools that both execute code and are installed in the image: 6 (`go-test-race`, `node-trace-uncaught`, `python-faulthandler`, `eslint`, `go-vet`, `go-native-fuzz`) plus the internal Python probe (needs no binaries, produces the primary proof). The other ~17 are missing because their toolchains are missing (Rust, .NET, LLVM, valgrind) — installing them is an image-weight decision, already at 2.58 GB.

**Evidence type is not chosen by the tool's flag.** `eslint`/`go-vet` carry `executes_project_code:true` because they load the project's own config/plugins, not because they run the program — they stay `STATIC_ANALYZER`. Only something that actually observes a program running earns `RUNTIME_DETECTOR`, and a `replay_plan` returned by the toolpack promotes it to `DETERMINISTIC_REPRODUCER`. No automatic transition beyond `HYPOTHESIZED` — the module supplies the proof, the decision to act on it stays with whoever takes it.

**Evidence.** 86 green checks (17 sandbox + 13 e2e + 28 memory + 28 HTTP). Live: `CONFIRMED` reached on an imported copy; data intact; `docker stop` exit 0 on both containers (D-0286 unregressed). Rollback containers held: `debug-evolution-pre-cube-memory`, `debug-evolution-pre-sandbox`.
**Deploy.** `debug-evolution:1.2.0-sandbox-execution`, two containers.
**Status.** Installed and verified live. First `CONFIRMED` in the module's history.

## D-0290 · Debug Evolution was running under NOESAR's own uid — separated to a dedicated uid + one-file supplementary group — 2026-08-02

**Decision.** Measured, not guessed: `noesar-evolution` and `debug-evolution` both ran as **uid 10001**. NOESAR protects runtime secrets with owner-only modes — measured: 1908 files at `0600`, 55 dirs at `0700`, 3 at `0400` under `NOESAR_EVOLUTION_RUNTIME`/`SHADOWS`/`NOESAR/config/secrets` — and "owner-only" means nothing between two processes the kernel considers the same user. The module could read every credential in the vault, not just its own; nobody had exploited it, it simply was never a boundary.

**Why identity, not a mask.** Hiding today's sensitive folders is a snapshot — the next secret written somewhere unanticipated would be silently exposed. Same logic already written in `scan.py::read_only_mounts()`, which derives from `/proc/mounts` instead of keeping a list ("a fixed list would be wrong the first time an install mounts something else"). This reaches beyond this one module: Debug Evolution is the reference sector-module, and every future module inherits the isolation established here.

**The constraint that decided the shape.** NOESAR runs non-root, so it cannot `chown` a file to a different uid. What it can do: `chmod` a file it owns, and `chgrp` to a group it belongs to. Hence: the module gets its own **uid/gid 10010** with **supplementary group 10001**, its token at `0640`, its directory at `0710` (traversable, not listable). Verified before choosing this over recreating the NOESAR container: none of the 1966 protected paths grant read to group 10001 (the only group-readable tree is `SHADOWS`, group 10002 = `atomd`) — so the shared group buys exactly one file and nothing else.

**Evidence.** 0/1966 protected files readable by the module; exact-path reads denied on all 5 sensitive targets; `ls` of the credentials directory denied; `.tools` = 0 entries; the module's own token reads fine. Runner: uid 10010 without group 10001, network `none` (LAN, internal network and Internet all unreachable), mounts only the sandbox volume. Data intact (DB SHA256 identical before/after, 19 projects, 3100 findings). A real scan on `STATS_HUB` (previously invisible) — `DONE` 7/7, 2 findings; a real `ruff FINDINGS`. Clean stops, exit 0 (D-0286's SIGTERM unregressed).
**Intended side effect.** `/mnt/cachec:ro` mounted under `workspace/programmi` — the picker now sees 37 programs instead of 2, new ones appearing on their own without recreating the container.
**Deploy.** Verified live on `noesar-evolution` and `debug-evolution` s305; the `server.mjs` source change (`grantTokenToModule()`, `0710` dir, `0640` token) was applied by hand to the running filesystem first and re-verified present in the built image as of the D-0294 single-lineage rebuild (checked live in this session, 2026-08-03: `grantTokenToModule()` and the `0o710`/`0o640` modes are in the running container's `server.mjs`).
**Status.** Installed and verified live.

## D-0291 · Target attachment, points B and D — SSH targets in the module's console without the key ever crossing it; network shares via `/mnt/remotes` — 2026-08-02

**Decision (point B — SSH targets).** D-0286 had established that Debug Evolution never sees an SSH credential — NOESAR runs `ssh-keyscan`/`scp`, the module receives a tarball. Putting the target screens inside the module's own console would have undone that: a private key pasted by the Owner would pass through the module's process. Fixed with a `/noesar-api/` prefix in `module-console-proxy.mjs` that the proxy answers itself instead of forwarding to the module: it strips the prefix and sends the request to NOESAR's own listener **with the session cookie intact** (everywhere else the proxy still does `delete headers.cookie`). The key travels browser → NOESAR; the module only draws the screen and holds nothing. The non-obvious enabler: `noesar_csrf` is a **non-HttpOnly** cookie (`auth.mjs:675`) and cookies are not port-separated, so JS served on port 8089 can read it and put it back in the `x-noesar-csrf` header; the module's CSP (`connect-src 'self'`) covers the call because it is same-origin. 5 new tests in `module-console-proxy.test.mjs` with two fake upstreams that echo what they actually receive, confirming `/noesar-api/` reaches NOESAR prefix-stripped with the cookie present, every other path reaches the module without the cookie, and a path merely containing the prefix without starting with it is not hijacked.

**Decision (point D — network shares).** Neither NOESAR nor the module can mount SMB/NFS themselves (`--cap-drop ALL`, read-only rootfs, `mount()` needs `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`). But Unraid mounts remote shares under `/mnt/remotes` (Unassigned Devices plugin) — exactly the "add a network path" flow the Owner described. Mounted read-only into `workspace/rete`. The trap that would have made this silently useless: Docker bind mounts are `rprivate`, so a share mounted *after* the container starts would not appear — `/mnt/remotes` on the host is `shared:3`, so the mount had to be `:ro,rslave`. Verified live by mounting a fake share into an already-running container: it appeared without recreating anything, the picker saw it, a scan found `DONE` 2/2 files, and it vanished on `umount`.

**Status.** Both points installed and verified live. Point C (API targets) remained open at the end of this decision — see D-0292.

## D-0292 · Target attachment, point C — API targets, the one place the module handles a live credential — 2026-08-02

**Decision.** For SSH, NOESAR could hold the credential and hand the module a file. For APIs the same trick does not exist: `remote-api.pyz` is a Python zipapp and **NOESAR has no `python3`** (measured on the live container: `openssl`/`ssh`/`scp`/`tar`/`node` are present, `python3` and `curl` are not). Putting a Python runtime inside NOESAR just to keep a token out would put the toolpack on the wrong side of the module boundary. So: NOESAR remains the only place the credential is **stored**; the module is where it is **used**, for the duration of one probe — a weaker property than SSH's, not claimed equivalent, and a different kind of secret besides: an SSH key opens a whole machine and is only the *means*; an API token is the thing **under examination**. The probe goes over the toolpack's `rpc` verb (JSON-per-line on stdin) rather than its CLI, because the CLI takes the credential as a `--header` argument, readable from `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` — `rpc` keeps the secret out of `argv` entirely. A target becomes a synthetic project, `api://host:port`, with findings carrying the URL as `path` — Evidence Court, the 6 agents, cube memory and SARIF all work unmodified because identity is the URL, not a registry row.

**A fabricated verdict found by using it, not by reading it.** Every non-zero exit from the TLS probe was read as "certificate verification failed" — including a probe the toolpack's own policy had *refused to run* (private address, no grant), which then produced a fabricated `HIGH` finding about a certificate nobody had looked at. Fixed: only `SSLCertVerificationError` (→ `DE-API-TLS-UNTRUSTED`) and an `https://` port answering in cleartext (→ `DE-API-TLS-ABSENT`) are findings; a policy refusal, a DNS failure, or a closed port are steps, not evidence. Two chained defects followed: "no step succeeded" was silently read as success with zero findings ("saw nothing" and "nothing wrong" collapsed into one) — now raises instead; and the first fix had been discarding `DE-API-TLS-ABSENT`, whose proof *is* that every step failed.

**Two real defects the Owner found on first real use, not caught by tests.** (1) The "last probe" panel lied: a *failed* probe updated only the status line and left the previous probe's steps standing, so a refusal looked like another target's success — the panel now clears before the request starts and the status line names the target. (2) `protected_path: "/"` crashed the module (`500 IntegrityError`) — `urljoin(base, '')` returns the base, so the endpoint list contained the same URL twice and genome nodes (keyed by URL) collided on a primary key. Fixed by deduplicating the list, not by rejecting `/` — "is the root reachable without a credential" is a legitimate question to ask.

**Evidence.** Toolpack authorizations are fields on the target, not call-time parameters — the Owner decides once, all `false` on an absent field. No credential enters the findings DB, WAL, SHM, audit log, or `argv` — checked directly, not assumed. `record_sha256` from the toolpack lands in `artifact_sha256` as `RUNTIME_DETECTOR` evidence — a hash of the target, not a replay plan, so it corroborates but does not reproduce.
**Deploy.** Verified live against two real upstreams echoing what they received.
**Status.** Installed and verified live. This closed the Owner's 0→A→B→C→D target-attachment plan (0=D-0290, A=D-0290, B/D=D-0291, C=D-0292).

## D-0293 · Triage for a single finding, not a whole scan — 2026-08-02

**Decision.** The existing triage bridge could not judge one finding on demand, for two independent reasons: it filters `state == 'DETECTED'` while every probe/sandbox finding is born `HYPOTHESIZED`, and a scan launched just to judge one finding would have woken ATOM on every other `DETECTED` finding in the installation too. New route: `POST /api/v1/debug-evolution/findings/:id/triage`, which only ever attempts the transition **from** `DETECTED` — `HYPOTHESIZED → HYPOTHESIZED` is not a legal edge, and asking for it would have failed the call *after* the evidence was already written, not before.
**Status.** Installed and verified live. Honest result on ATOM's own answer quality logged separately (`A-0023`, s306/s307).

## D-0294 · `oci/Dockerfile` builds this product again — 77 overlays folded into one file, proven by booting it — 2026-08-02
**A note on the number.** This file jumps from `D-0287` to `D-0294`: `D-0288`…`D-0293` were
implemented, deployed and committed (commit `8cffeee`) but **never written into this log** —
they exist only in that commit message. Not reconstructed here from summaries, because writing
six decision records from memory would be inventing the very thing this file is for. Named so
it is not mistaken for a gap in the work.

**Decision.** `oci/Dockerfile` is rewritten as a single-lineage build of the running product:
a `rust:1-bookworm` builder stage for both peers (`noesar-supervisord`, `noesar-sandbox`, one
stage instead of the two the overlays used), the pinned pgdg install of PostgreSQL
`18.4-1.pgdg12+1` and pgvector `0.8.5-1.pgdg12+1`, the exact file set the image actually
carries, the full `ENV`, and `ENTRYPOINT ["/opt/noesar/bin/noesar-supervisord"]`. A
`.dockerignore` is added — nothing it excludes is referenced by any `COPY`. Two labels the live
image carries, `org.noesar.base-image` and `org.noesar.flatten`, are deliberately dropped: they
describe a lineage a single-file build does not have, and copying them would re-record a false
history on a fresh artefact.

**Why.** `D-0271` found this file builds a *different system* — no PostgreSQL, `reference-json`
data plane, `node server.mjs` as entrypoint. s308 measured why it had become unrecoverable:
the overlay chain reached **127 of overlay2's 128 layers** at
`noesar-evolution:phase4-update-signing-side` and was rescued by flattening, and **flattening
severs source from artefact** — the live image's history is 1 `RUN`, 24 `COPY`, 48 `LABEL` and
one 819 MB layer with no recorded instruction. The ability to rebuild this product did not live
in this repository; it lived in ~82 image tags on one host's Docker daemon, one `docker image
prune` from gone. The recovered instructions are preserved as evidence in `oci/lineage/`.

**Rejected.** Copying `capabilities/`, `schemas/` and `docs/` as whole directories: the running
image holds 2 files under `capabilities/` and 4 under `schemas/` where this repository holds 43
of each, so directory copies would ship files the product has never contained. Checked against
the live image, not inferred. Also rejected: writing the file and reviewing it instead of
building it — an unverified Dockerfile is the class of artefact this project refuses.

**Evidence.** Built, then compared against `noesar-evolution:phase4-court-triage`, the image
running in production: `/opt/noesar` holds **295 files in both, `diff` empty**, and **294 of
295 are identical byte for byte by sha256**. The one that differs is `package.json`, and the
difference is a finding, not an error: it was copied once at the first build and never again in
77 overlays, so the *live* image is missing three `npm` scripts this repository has. 24 layers
against 26, 829 MB against 864 MB. Booted on a throwaway container with an empty volume:
**healthy in 10 s**, all three ARCH-001 peers spawned (`postgres`, `api`, `codev`), PostgreSQL
18.4 with pgvector 0.8.5, **19 migrations applied**, `/livez` and `/healthz` both `200`.

**The half that was missing everywhere, found by booting it.** The first boot attempt came up
`running` and **`unhealthy`** with PostgreSQL perfectly fine: the api peer died five times on
`listen EACCES: permission denied /run/codev-peer.sock`. The live container runs `--read-only`
with `--tmpfs /run:...,mode=1777` and `--tmpfs /tmp`, and that **`mode=1777` is load-bearing** —
uid 10001 cannot create its socket in a root-owned `/run`. None of it was in the image, the
repository, or any document: **this image has never been able to boot the product on its own,
and nothing said so.** The run contract is now written at the top of `oci/Dockerfile`.

**Reversal cost.** Was none while undeployed. Now that it is deployed: low and local — the
previous container is kept stopped, not removed, as `noesar-evolution-old-court-triage`, and
the previous `oci/Dockerfile` is one `git revert` away.
**Status.** **Built, proven and deployed live on Owner authorization.** Container recreated
from `noesar-evolution:single-lineage-rebuild` with `HostConfig`/env/healthcheck read back out
of the running container, not retyped: same fixed IP `172.22.0.5` on `noesar-evolution-net`,
uid `10001:10001`, `--read-only`, `--tmpfs /run:mode=1777` and `--tmpfs /tmp`, `--cap-drop ALL`,
both port bindings (`8100`, `8089`), both workspace/shadows binds, `restart=unless-stopped`.
Healthy in **~6 s**. Verified live: `/livez` and `/healthz` both `200` on `192.168.178.100:8100`,
`atomd` and `debug-evolution` unaffected (`healthy`), all three ARCH-001 peers
(`postgres`, `api`, `codev`) running inside `noesar-supervisord`. Previous container kept
stopped as `noesar-evolution-old-court-triage` for rollback. The three `npm` scripts this image
adds over the live one (`test:accessibility`, `test:installers`,
`test:installers-cross-platform`) were checked before deploying: dev/test-only, not on any
runtime path, so their absence from the old image was never a regression. Not fixed by this
deploy, carried over unchanged: the stray
`services/reference-control-plane/src/server.mjs.bak_pre_uid_separation_20260802T000554Z` in
the image.

## D-0295 · Passkey (WebAuthn) as an alternative to TOTP in the second login factor — 2026-08-03

**Decision.** A passkey now satisfies stage 2 of login exactly where a TOTP code did —
Owner's choice: `TOTP oppure passkey`, not passwordless and not an additional factor
stacked on top of both. Scoped narrowly to what the Owner authorised: attestation `none`
(no attestation certificate chain), algorithm ES256 (P-256) only, and the ceremony bound to
the SAME `loginChallenge` the password step already minted — a passkey assertion cannot be
replayed onto a different login attempt. Registering or removing a passkey still requires
`#assertPresence` (password AND a live TOTP code), never a passkey alone: TOTP stays
mandatory at enrolment for `owner`/`admin` and is never dropped by adding a passkey, so the
stronger, already-established factor always exists to govern what a passkey can do.

**Why.** Thread 2, open since s297, scoped in s310 (three product questions: role of the
passkey, attestation depth, algorithm set) and answered by the Owner in s311. NOESAR
EVOLUTION carries zero npm dependencies by design — there is no `@simplewebauthn/server`
here. `webauthn.mjs` is a from-scratch CBOR (RFC 8949, definite-length subset only — CTAP2
authenticators never emit indefinite-length items) and COSE→JWK decoder, plus
`verifyRegistration`/`verifyAssertion` on `node:crypto`. WebAuthn ES256 assertion signatures
are ASN.1 DER-encoded ECDSA, which is `crypto.verify`'s default encoding, so no re-encoding
step was needed. A signature counter that fails to increase is refused as a clone signal,
*except* when it is `0` on both sides — most platform authenticators backed by a secure
enclave do not implement one at all, re-verifying the user by biometric/PIN on every use
instead, and that case is not comparable.

**Rejected.** A separate WebAuthn challenge parallel to the login's own: reusing the
existing `loginChallenges` record ties the two ceremonies together for free and rules out a
class of replay this project would otherwise have had to defend by hand. Extending
`#assertPresence` itself to accept a passkey in place of TOTP for step-up actions
(`changePassword`, `beginMfaReplacement`, `regenerateRecoveryCodes`): out of the scope the
Owner authorised — "sostituisce il TOTP nel secondo fattore di login" names login, not every
place TOTP is checked, and TOTP remaining permanently enrolled for MFA-required roles made
this a real choice, not a gap.

**Evidence.** Unit: **1553/1554** (`test/webauthn.test.mjs`, new, 33 tests — RFC 8949
Appendix A CBOR vectors plus WebAuthn fixtures built with a CBOR *encoder* that exists only
in the test, since production code only ever needs to decode what a browser sends; covers
registration/assertion rejection paths: wrong challenge, wrong origin, non-`none`
attestation, non-ES256 algorithm, RP ID mismatch, missing user verification, stale/replayed
signature counter, tampered signature, wrong public key, ceremony-type confusion). The one
pre-existing skip is unchanged. Built (`oci/Dockerfile`, unmodified) as
`noesar-evolution:passkey-webauthn-test`, healthy in ~7 s. **Proven live in isolation**
first — separate container, separate port, separate workspace, never connected to
production — with a Node script playing the browser's role: a genuine P-256 keypair signs
real CBOR/COSE structures over real HTTP against the running image. 13/13 checks: owner
setup, password login, passkey registration, **login on the passkey alone with no TOTP
code**, authenticated session from that login, **a replayed signature counter refused
(`401`)**, a correctly incremented counter on the same login attempt accepted, passkey
removal, and login options correctly refusing after removal (`404`, no passkey left).

**Reversal cost.** Was none while undeployed. Now that it is deployed: low and local, same
shape as `D-0294` — the previous container is kept stopped, not removed, and the previous
image tag is unaffected.

**Status.** **Built, proven live and deployed on Owner authorization**, all three steps
separately authorised in the same session (s311). Container recreated from
`noesar-evolution:single-lineage-rebuild` with `HostConfig`/env/healthcheck read back out of
the running container: same fixed IP `172.22.0.5` on `noesar-evolution-net`, uid
`10001:10001`, `--read-only`, `--tmpfs /run:mode=1777` and `--tmpfs /tmp`, `--cap-drop ALL`,
both port bindings (`8100`, `8089`), both workspace/shadows binds, `restart=unless-stopped`.
Healthy in **~7 s**. Verified live: `/livez` and `/healthz` both `200` on
`192.168.178.100:8100`, the owner account's existing data intact on the persistent volume,
`atomd`/`debug-evolution`/`debug-evolution-runner` unaffected. A smoke test against the real
production route with a bogus login challenge returned a clean `401`, not a `500` — the real
owner's credentials were not available in this session, so a full passkey login against
production data was not attempted. Previous container kept stopped as
`noesar-evolution-old-single-lineage-rebuild` for rollback.

## D-0296 · Thread 4 (Block G) scoped: Owner Bootstrap re-verified, internal security review found and fixed a real DoS in the new WebAuthn code — 2026-08-03

**Decision.** Block G, open since s297 and never scoped in detail, is defined in
`docs/SESSION_HANDOFF.md` as "Owner Bootstrap+pentest" — the last block of the Owner's
7-part plan, marked "obbligatoria, non automatizzabile" from the start. Scoped with the
Owner via `AskUserQuestion` rather than guessed at, because its two halves are not the
same kind of work: Owner Bootstrap is a documentation/re-verification task, an
independent penetration test is not something this assistant can perform — "independent"
means an external party by definition. The Owner selected three of four options: (1)
update and re-verify Owner Bootstrap, (2) an internal security self-assessment (explicitly
not a substitute for group 6 of `PRODUCTION_READINESS_V050.md`), (3) bookkeeping to reflect
the real current state.

**Owner Bootstrap.** `docs/OWNER_BOOTSTRAP.md` corrected — it told operators to "treat
passkey/WebAuthn as still missing", false since `D-0295`. Replaced with the real MFA
relationship: TOTP enrolment is still mandatory and unskippable at first setup; a passkey
can be added afterward and from then on works in place of a TOTP code at login, but
registering or removing one still requires proving presence with password+TOTP. The whole
flow was then re-verified live end to end on a disposable probe container (the running
production container was never touched): token file `0600`/`10001:10001` with a
fingerprint matching the startup log, setup refused both without a token and with a wrong
one, both refusals landing in the audit ledger as `auth.setup-denied` (not just the
operational log — a distinct file, checked directly), only the token PATH ever in the
container environment, a second setup attempt refused `409` once initialized, password
alone answering `mfaRequired:true` with no session cookie issued, a wrong TOTP code
refused, a correct one logging in `role:owner`/`mfaEnabled:true` with
`HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict` cookies (confirmed from raw response headers, not inferred),
and an owner-only route answering `200` with the session and `401` without one. Every
claim in the document's "What was verified" section reconfirmed against the current image,
not carried forward from memory.

**Internal security review — one real defect found and fixed.** `/security-review` could
not run as a skill: this session's working directory is pinned to `/mnt/cachec/NOESAR`,
one level above the git repository, and does not persist a `cd` between tool calls, so the
skill's own git-repository check always failed. Reviewed the pending, uncommitted WebAuthn
diff manually instead, with the same adversarial standard. **Found and fixed**: the CBOR
decoder (`webauthn.mjs`) had no upper bound on declared array/map length beyond the
buffer's own size, and it is reached from `POST /api/v1/auth/login/passkey` —
unauthenticated by necessity, since it IS the login step. Any account holder can
self-register a passkey (an ordinary, intended action) and thereby learn their own real
`credentialId`; logging out and POSTing that `credentialId` with an oversized, malformed
`authenticatorData` reaches the decoder before any signature check. Measured before the
fix: a 20 MB payload (well inside the existing 64 MB body cap) blocked the single Node
event loop for **656 ms**, scaling linearly (100 K items = 8.5 ms, 1 M = 47.5 ms, 5 M =
180.7 ms, 20 M = 655.8 ms) — because `noesar-supervisord` runs the api peer as one process
(`ARCH-001`), that block stalls every concurrent user, not just the caller. A sustained
sequence of such requests is a full pre-auth denial of service against the whole instance.
**Fixed** with an 8 KiB cap on every WebAuthn binary field (`clientDataJSON`,
`attestationObject`, `authenticatorData`, `signature`), checked before any CBOR/JSON
parsing — real payloads for `attestation:'none'`/ES256 are under 300 bytes, so the cap
costs nothing legitimate. Re-measured after the fix: the same 20 MB payload now rejects in
**12.9 ms** (Node's native base64url decode of the oversized string, unavoidable, but ~50×
less blocking time and no longer a practical attack at any realistic rate). Two regression
tests added asserting rejection happens in under 50 ms. This is evidence toward
`PRODUCTION_READINESS_V050.md` group 6, not a substitute for it — a self-review is not an
independent one.

**Bookkeeping.** `docs/PRODUCTION_READINESS_V050.md` now states plainly that group 6
(independent penetration test) is the one gate this project cannot close by writing code.

**Rejected.** Attempting to simulate an "independent" pentest myself: the word means an
external party, and pretending otherwise would misrepresent the gate as satisfied when it
is not — the same category of dishonesty this project has refused before (`classify`/
`confidence`/`expect` mislabeling model opinion as tool-verified evidence, `D-0285`).

**Evidence.** Unit: **1555/1556** (`webauthn.test.mjs` 35/35, +2 net — the size-cap
regressions — the one pre-existing skip unchanged). Timing measured directly with
`process.hrtime.bigint()`, not estimated.

**Status.** Owner Bootstrap doc corrected and re-verified live (probe container removed
after). Security defect found, fixed, tested, and **built** (`noesar-evolution:passkey-
webauthn-dos-fix`, healthy). Proven live over real HTTP on a disposable probe, not just
the unit import: registered a genuine passkey, then sent the same 20 MB hostile
`authenticatorData` to the real running `POST /api/v1/auth/login/passkey` — **251.8 ms**,
down from 656 ms measured at the decoder level pre-fix. Isolated where that residual comes
from before calling it done: the identical oversized payload sent to a wholly unrelated
route that never touches `webauthn.mjs` (`POST /api/v1/auth/login`) cost **152.9 ms** —
confirming the remainder is this product's existing, shared 64 MB body-read/JSON.parse
cost on every POST route, not a WebAuthn-specific residual. The fix closes exactly the
part that was newly, unboundedly attacker-controlled (CBOR decode cost scaling with
attacker-chosen structure); the small fixed remainder is a pre-existing, whole-product
characteristic, out of scope for this fix. **Not yet deployed**: the running production
container (`noesar-evolution:passkey-webauthn-test`, from `D-0295`) still carries the
unpatched decoder — redeploying needs its own authorization, the same pattern as every
deploy this session.

---

**Addendum to `D-0296`, 2026-08-03 (s314).** The paragraph above says the fix was "not yet
deployed" and names `noesar-evolution:passkey-webauthn-test` as what production carries.
That is no longer true and is left standing rather than rewritten, per this log's habit of
correcting by note. Measured at the start of s314, from the live daemon and not from a
document: `noesar-evolution` is `Up 12 hours (healthy)` on
**`noesar-evolution:passkey-webauthn-dos-fix`** — the patched image. (`CLAUDE.md`'s own
container table still named `passkey-webauthn-test` too; corrected in the same session.)

## D-0297 · CodeN Evolution, phase 1 of 5: the workbench's sixteen panels become addresses, and three labels stop lying — 2026-08-03

**Context.** The Owner asked in s311 for graphic work on CodeN Evolution, scoped in s313 to
the `#/coden` route inside this product (not CodeN Ultra), and accepted a design there: the
Navigator column, the bench tabs and the agent-column menu — three separate navigation
widgets the Owner found to be "too many menus" — are to be replaced by a single
jump-to-address mechanism on `/`, identical in the WebUI and the TUI. s314 begins the
implementation as a five-phase programme, each phase gated on the Owner's authorization.
This is phase 1: **nothing can be jumped to before it has an address.**

**Correction to the s313 premise, measured before writing code.** s313 recorded the TUI as
"not built" and estimated it as a new client plus a new protocol. It is neither. It exists
and it runs: `tools/tui-client.mjs` (474 lines, zero dependencies), the server half in
`src/session-protocol.mjs`, and the externally reachable socket owned by the separate
`codev` process (`bin/codev-child.mjs`, `ARCH-001`). Driven live during this session, it
answered `Connected — protocol noesar-tui/1` and then refused a bad credential. The
estimate for the TUI phase drops accordingly; the label was the only thing missing.

**Decision.** The eleven bench panels and five agent panels are two regions of one address
space — `#/coden/bench/diff`, `#/coden/agent/plan` — carried by the same three hash
segments Settings and Sessions already use. Three properties are load-bearing:

1. **The panel names are not written in the router.** They are read from the markup's own
   `data-bench-panel`/`data-agent-panel` attributes. A hand-kept list beside the markup is
   precisely how the sidebar came to advertise the TUI as "not built" for as long as the
   TUI had been working: two copies of one fact, one of them maintained.
2. **A tab click moves the address with `history.pushState`, not `location.hash=`.**
   Assigning the hash fires `hashchange`, which re-runs `VIEW_LOADERS.coden` — a round of
   requests per tab click. `pushState` is silent, and the Back button still fires
   `hashchange` when it traverses two different hashes, so the history stays real. Measured
   in the browser: 19 → 19 requests to `/api/v1/` across a tab click.
3. **Completing or correcting an address is not a navigation.** A bare `#/coden` is
   completed with the panel actually showing, and a panel name nobody has falls back to the
   default *and takes the address with it*; both are written with `replaceState`, which
   fires nothing and leaves no redundant entry in the Back button's way.

**Three false claims removed, all of them the interface contradicting its own code:** the
`not built` flag (the destination's own page says `SESSION PROTOCOL BUILT`, correctly); the
workaround in `app.js` that deleted the string `not built` out of a panel title, which
would have gone on silently absorbing the next stale flag; and the Sessions keyboard map,
which taught a slash-prefixed terminal vocabulary (`/sessions`, `/archive <n>`,
`/select <n…>`) that `tui-client.mjs` has never answered to. The last one also mattered
forward: `/` is about to become the jump-to-address key, and a documented command starting
with `/` would have given one key two meanings.

**A defect in this phase's own code, found by the browser and by nothing else.** The
address correction was gated on `activate()`'s `updateHash` flag — which `goToHash()`
passes as `false` for everything except a legacy redirect. The correction was therefore
dead code for every address a person can type: `#/coden` never completed, and a misspelt
panel fell back on screen while the address went on naming a panel that does not exist.
Eleven structural tests passed throughout. Corrections are now ungated; only navigation
still honours the flag.

**Verification.** `npm test` 1566/1567 (0 fail, 1 pre-existing skip: the sandbox binary is
not built for this host), of which 11 new in
`test/coden-addressable-panels.test.mjs`; ESLint 299 files, 0/0/0. Each new assertion was
self-tested by reintroducing the defect it guards — seven mutations, seven failures, one
per mutation, sources restored byte-identically. Browser acceptance on a disposable probe:
**351/351**, including a cold deep link (a reload, because `page.goto` to a hash-only
difference never reloads the document — the first version of the check called a
same-document hash change a deep link and would have reported PASS on an untested case),
the request count across a tab click, and the Back button. Two failures that run surfaced
were pre-existing and are fixed here rather than in the phase that caused them: the
Settings section count had been asserted as fourteen since `D-0291` made it fifteen, and
the legacy-redirect check compared hashes exactly, which a completed address no longer
matches.

**Not deployed.** The running container is untouched; this is source only.

## D-0298 · CodeN Evolution, phase 2 of 5: `/` goes to an address — in the box that already existed, not in a new one — 2026-08-03

**Decision, and the one that mattered.** The accepted s313 design says `/` opens a filterable
list of every destination. The obvious build is a command-palette overlay, and it would have
been the wrong one: the top bar already carries a search box, on Ctrl K, so an overlay would
have ADDED a navigation widget while the Owner's whole objection was how many there are
(s313: three small tidy menus still read as "too many menus" — the count of interaction
points, not the density of each). The mechanism therefore goes where the box already is.
`/` and Ctrl K both reach it; the only difference is which key you happen to know.

The box now answers with two kinds of thing and never conflates them: **addresses** — all 46
of them, matched locally with no network, drawn on the first keystroke because a jump that
waits for a round trip is not a jump — and **content**, what `/api/v1/search` finds inside
those addresses, debounced as before.

**The address list is read off the interface, never written beside it** — the same
single-copy rule `D-0297` established. It comes from the sidebar's own buttons, the Settings
menu's own entries, and the bench and agent panels' own attributes. Two things fall out of
that beyond staleness: a destination `applyNavAccess()` has hidden from this account is
`hidden` in the DOM and therefore simply absent, so the box cannot offer a page whose every
request would answer 403; and phase 3 can retire the Navigator column without touching a
line of this code.

`/` is guarded by the same `isTyping()` the sidebar's `[` and `]` already use — one guard,
not a second opinion about what counts as typing. Verified in the browser by typing
"and/or" into the chat composer: the phrase arrives whole and nothing opens.

**A dead control, removed.** The content rows were rendered as `<button>` with no handler on
them at all — eight kinds of result, every one a control that did nothing when clicked. They
lead somewhere now: to the destination that OWNS that kind of thing, which is as far as this
product can honestly go, since nothing here has a per-item address yet. The row says which
page it opens rather than implying it will select the item, and a test reads the eight types
out of `workspace-service.mjs` itself, so a ninth type fails the suite instead of shipping
as another dead row.

**A real defect found while wiring it, and fixed: a project scope hid every project.** The
box showed nothing for a query the same endpoint answered with two results. Measured, not
guessed: a project record carries no `projectId` of its own, so `globalSearch`'s scope
filter `item.projectId===projectId` excluded every project whenever one was selected — you
could not search your way to the project you wanted to switch to, or find the one you were
already in. A project is not INSIDE a project, so the scope no longer filters projects;
scoping remains about what a project contains, and an artifact belonging elsewhere still
stays out. The pre-existing test missed it by asserting a disjunction —
`some(['project','artifact','message'])` — which went on passing on the artifact while
`project` was never returned at all.

**Reported, not fixed: the same shape mismatch hides messages.** A message record carries
`conversationId` and no `projectId`, so a project scope drops every message too. Unlike a
project, a message really is inside a project — through its conversation — so here the
filter means to keep it and the data shape defeats it. Resolving conversation→project per
record is a different change with its own cost; it is measured and named here rather than
smuggled into a navigation phase. The test says so in place of asserting it, because a test
must not bless a defect.

**Verification.** `npm test` 1578/1579 (0 fail, 1 pre-existing skip), 11 new in
`test/webui-jump-to-address.test.mjs` plus 1 in `ai-workspace.test.mjs`; ESLint 0/0/0. Six
mutations, six failures, one each — including reverting the search fix and removing the
`/` typing guard, and one mutation that had to be redone because the first version of it
patched the sidebar's identical guard instead of this one. Browser acceptance **365/365**,
which is where the keyboard, the focus and the ARIA wiring are actually proven: `/` opens
with 46 addresses and does not leak into the box as text, typing ranks `coden/bench/diff`
first, `aria-activedescendant` names the highlighted row while focus stays in the input,
Enter goes and closes, Escape closes, Ctrl K still opens, and a content row click lands on
`#/projects`.

**Not deployed.** Source only; the running container is untouched.

## D-0299 · CodeN Evolution, phase 3 of 5: three navigation widgets become none — 2026-08-03

**Decision.** The Navigator column, the eleven bench tabs and the five-entry agent menu are
removed from the workbench. This is the change the Owner actually asked for in s313 — the
first two phases existed to make it possible without losing anything. The complaint was
never that the three were untidy: `D-0236`/`D-0237` had already made the agent column
compact, and it was still rejected, because what is felt is the NUMBER of navigation widgets
standing open at once, not the density of each.

**Nothing they reached stopped being reachable.** The eleven bench panels and the five agent
panels have had addresses since `D-0297`. The Navigator's nine groups did not, and this is
where they get them: they are bench panels now — same ids, same lists, same cap of six, the
same renderer filling them — reached by name like everything else instead of standing
permanently open in a column beside the work. The bench grid drops from three columns to
two so no gap is left where the column was.

**One visible affordance is left, and it deliberately holds no list.** A breadcrumb naming
the panel that is open (`CodeN Evolution · Diff`), which opens the top bar's box with
`/coden/` already typed — the same 25 addresses, filtered to this page. It is not a menu: it
owns no destinations of its own, so it cannot drift from the list the box builds out of the
interface. Without it `/` would be the only way to change panel, and this product's own rule
— written beside the sidebar rank keys — is that a keyboard shortcut is the fast path and
never the only path.

**A second crop of dead controls, in the place the first one taught us to look.** The
Navigator's rows were `<button>` with no handler on them: seven lists of up to six entries,
none of which did anything when clicked — the same defect `D-0298` found in the search
results, in a second place. They now open the destination that owns that kind of thing and
say so in their title, and a test asserts every one of the seven lists passes a destination.

**An acceptance criterion re-formed, and said so rather than quietly relaxed.** `UI-030`
named three regions and `UI-032` eleven tabs; `webui-markup-structure.test.mjs` asserted
both. Their FORM is superseded by the Owner's design decision. Their SUBSTANCE is now
asserted more strictly than before: all twenty bench surfaces and all five agent panels are
listed by name, so a later move can re-form them again but cannot quietly drop one while a
test is loosened to allow it. The switchers staying gone is itself asserted.

**Verification.** `npm test` 1581/1582 (0 fail, 1 pre-existing skip), ESLint 0/0/0. Five
mutations, five failures — a tab put back, the breadcrumb removed, a list left without a
destination, a Navigator group renamed away, and the breadcrumb stopped from following the
panel. Browser acceptance **373/373**, including: the three widgets measured as zero pixels
on screen rather than merely absent from the markup, the bench computing to two columns, a
Navigator group reached by its own address and its rows leading to `#/projects`, and the
breadcrumb opening the box with exactly this page's 25 addresses in it.

Three failures in that run came from the harness driving the interface as it used to be —
the old blocks still clicked `[data-bench-tab]`, and two checks staged their state in ways
that the address COMPLETION defeats: `page.goto('#/coden')` rewrites the address to the
panel already showing before a reload can happen, and `/` is a character, not a shortcut,
while the box has focus. Each was the product behaving as designed and the driver assuming
otherwise; the driver was corrected, and the notes are in it.

**Not deployed.** Source only; the running container is untouched.

## D-0300 · CodeN Evolution, phase 4 of 5: the terminal stops keeping its own list — 2026-08-03

**Decision.** The `/` jump-to-address mechanism accepted in s313 now works in the terminal
shell, and it is the same mechanism rather than a second one that resembles it: the address
list is served over the session protocol (`coden.addresses`), derived from
`apps/webui-static/index.html` — the very file the browser builds its own list out of — by
the new `src/coden-address-book.mjs`. `tools/tui-client.mjs` carries no list of destinations
at all any more.

**Why this and not "add a `/` command".** The phase was scoped as "parity of `/` in the TUI",
which sounds like a feature to add. Reading the client first showed the actual defect:
`PANEL_NAMES` in `tui-client.mjs` declared **fourteen** panels against the markup's
**twenty-five**, with the bench's and the agent column's namespaces flattened into one and
eleven bench panels — Terminal, Problems, Projects, Recent, Sessions, Tasks, Agents, Tools,
Plugins, History, Favourites — simply absent. `DECLARED_EMPTY_PANELS` was a second such copy:
six placeholder texts hand-copied from the interface, of which the ones still quoted had
drifted from the paragraphs they claimed to be quoting. Nobody had noticed either, because a
list only ever compared to itself always agrees. That is the same defect phases 1–3 spent
